issues.summary: Add Support for Paypal and Apple Pay as Default Payment Methods
issues.description:
Summary

Currently, only credit cards can be set as default payment methods. This ticket adds support for PayPal Direct and Apple Pay to be set as default payment methods in customer wallets.

Background

The system currently restricts default payment methods to credit cards only (Payment Type ID = 2). This restriction is enforced in multiple layers:

- Wallet Service validation throws exception: "Only credit card wallet options can be set as the default"

- Legacy WalletService explicitly rejects PayPal and Apple Pay in switch statement

- Database layer only has SetDefaultCreditCardInWallet stored procedure

Both PayPal Direct (type 16) and Apple Pay (type 17) are already fully implemented payment types in the system with complete payment processing support.

Business Value

- Allows customers to use their preferred payment method as default

- Improves user experience for customers who prefer digital wallets

- Aligns with industry standards where any valid payment method can be default

---
Default Payment Method Support

What needs to work:

- Users can set PayPal Direct (Payment Type 16) as their default payment method

- Users can set Apple Pay (Payment Type 17) as their default payment method

- Only one payment method can be default at a time per wallet

- When a user sets a new default, the old one automatically gets unset

- All current validations should remain such as the inability to set an inactive or expired payment method as a default

- If this will require a contract change to the existing Get Wallet endpoint, please create a brand new wallet endpoint or find a way to make it backwards compatible

- It is not expected UI teams will be able to support this in parallel

Checkout Integration

Scheduled Payments

Recurring charges need to work:

- Scheduled payments should support PayPal and Apple Pay as defaults

- Subscription renewals should support PayPal and Apple Pay as defaults

Payment Operations

These operations need to handle PayPal/Apple Pay defaults:

- Refunds - should process correctly when refunding to a PayPal or Apple Pay default

- No-show charges - should work when charging a PayPal or Apple Pay default

- Manual charges - should work when charging a PayPal or Apple Pay default

---
Implementation Areas

1. Wallet Service - Core Default Payment Logic

What needs to change:

- Remove the restriction that only allows credit cards to be set as default

- Update validation logic to accept PayPal Direct and Apple Pay as valid default payment types

- Ensure database operations (stored procedures) can handle setting any payment type as default, not just credit cards

---
2. Customer Service Integration

What needs to verify:

- Ensure the service layer properly passes through PayPal and Apple Pay when setting defaults

- No additional restrictions or assumptions at this layer

---
3. TeeTimesAPI / API 2.1 Layer

What needs to change/verify:

- Customer wallet management endpoints (methods with names like "SetCreditCardAsPrimary" may need updating)

- Reservation creation logic when no payment method is specified (should fall back to default)

- Order creation logic when no payment method is specified (should fall back to default)

- Payment validation in reservation workflows

---
4. Reservation Service Workflows

What needs to verify:

- Payment validation activities accept PayPal and Apple Pay as defaults

- Charge building activities handle all payment types equally

- Payment capture activities work with PayPal and Apple Pay defaults

- Default payment retrieval logic doesn't assume credit cards

---
5. Scheduled Payments & Recurring Charges

What needs to verify:

- Scheduled payment execution can charge PayPal and Apple Pay defaults

- Subscription renewal workflows support PayPal and Apple Pay

- Payment method update workflows handle all payment types

- Background job processors don't assume credit cards

---
6. Refund Processing

What needs to verify:

- Refund workflows can process refunds to PayPal and Apple Pay

- Refund amount calculations work for all payment types

- Scheduled payment refunds handle all payment types

---
7. No-Show & Manual Charge Workflows

What needs to verify:

- No-show charge workflows can charge PayPal and Apple Pay defaults

- Manual charge workflows accept PayPal and Apple Pay

- Validation logic doesn't restrict to credit cards only

---
8. Database Layer

What needs to change:

- Create or update stored procedures to set defaults for any payment type (not just credit cards)

- Ensure the IsDefault flag works consistently across all payment types

- Database operations should be payment-type agnostic

---
9. Cross-Cutting Concerns to Review

Default Payment Retrieval:

- Anywhere the system fetches "the default payment method" to use automatically

- Ensure no code assumes the default will always be a credit card type

Payment Type Validation:

- Look for validation logic that checks payment types

- Ensure none inadvertently block PayPal or Apple Pay from being defaults

Method Naming:

- Methods with names like "SetCreditCardAsPrimary" should either be renamed or verified to handle all payment types

Error Handling:

- Ensure error messages make sense for all payment types

- No error messages that say "credit card" when they mean "payment method"

---
Testing Notes

Unit Tests Required

Test Suite 1: Wallet Service Validation

Location: Internal Services/GolfNow.Services.Wallet/GolfNow.Services.Wallet.UnitTests/

Tests to Add:

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_PayPalDirect_Success
- Arrange: Customer with active PayPal payment option
- Act: Call SetDefaultWalletOption with PayPal wallet option ID
- Assert: Returns true, no exception thrown

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_ApplePay_Success
- Arrange: Customer with active Apple Pay payment option
- Act: Call SetDefaultWalletOption with Apple Pay wallet option ID
- Assert: Returns true, no exception thrown

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_ExpiredPayPal_Fails
- Arrange: Customer with expired PayPal payment option
- Act: Call SetDefaultWalletOption with expired PayPal ID
- Assert: Throws WalletInvalidDataException with appropriate message

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_GuestWallet_PayPal_Fails
- Arrange: Guest wallet with PayPal payment option
- Act: Call SetDefaultWalletOption
- Assert: Throws exception about guest wallets

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_SwitchFromCreditCardToPayPal
- Arrange: Customer with credit card as default
- Act: Set PayPal as default
- Assert: Credit card IsDefault = false, PayPal IsDefault = true

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_SwitchFromPayPalToApplePay
- Arrange: Customer with PayPal as default
- Act: Set Apple Pay as default
- Assert: PayPal IsDefault = false, Apple Pay IsDefault = true

Test Suite 2: Customer Service Integration

Location: Internal Services/GolfNow.Services.Customer/GolfNow.Services.Customer.UnitTests/

Tests to Add:

Test_SetDefaultPaymentOption_PayPal_IntegrationSuccess
Test_SetDefaultPaymentOption_ApplePay_IntegrationSuccess
Test_GetCustomerWallet_DefaultPayPalMarkedCorrectly
Test_GetCustomerWallet_DefaultApplePayMarkedCorrectly

Integration Tests Required

Test Scenario 1: Full Reservation Flow with Default PayPal

Setup:

- Create test customer with PayPal payment method

- Set PayPal as default via API

- Create reservation without specifying payment method

Expected Results:

- Reservation created successfully

- Payment charged to PayPal account

- Reservation payment_method_type = 16 (PayPal Direct)

- Charge record shows PayPal wallet option ID

Test Scenario 2: Full Reservation Flow with Default Apple Pay

Setup:

- Create test customer with Apple Pay payment method

- Set Apple Pay as default via API

- Create reservation without specifying payment method

Expected Results:

- Reservation created successfully

- Payment charged to Apple Pay account

- Reservation payment_method_type = 17 (Apple Pay)

- Charge record shows Apple Pay wallet option ID

Test Scenario 3: Scheduled Payment Execution

Setup:

- Create customer with scheduled payment

- Customer has PayPal as default payment method

- Trigger scheduled payment execution

Expected Results:

- Scheduled payment charges PayPal account

- Transaction records show PayPal as payment method

- No errors logged

Test Scenario 4: Refund to PayPal Default

Setup:

- Complete reservation with default PayPal

- Process full refund

Expected Results:

- Refund processes successfully

- Refund goes to original PayPal account

- Refund status updated correctly

Test Scenario 5: No-Show Charge

Setup:

- Create reservation with default Apple Pay

- Mark reservation as no-show

- Process no-show charge

Expected Results:

- No-show charge processes to Apple Pay account

- Charge successful

- Reservation status updated

Test Scenario 6: Multi-Currency Support

Setup:

- Set PayPal as default for customer in USD market

- Set PayPal as default for customer in CAD market

- Make reservations in both currencies

Expected Results:

- Both process successfully with correct currency

Manual QA Test Cases

QA-1: Basic Set Default Functionality

Steps:

- Login as customer with multiple payment methods (CC, PayPal, Apple Pay)

- Navigate to payment methods page

- Set PayPal as default

- Refresh page

- Verify PayPal shows as default

- Set Apple Pay as default

- Verify only Apple Pay shows as default

Expected: UI correctly shows default indicator, only one method is default at a time

QA-2: Reservation Without Specifying Payment

Steps:

- Set PayPal as default payment method

- Start new reservation booking

- Proceed to payment WITHOUT selecting a payment method

- Complete booking

Expected: Booking uses PayPal by default, confirmation shows PayPal

QA-3: Guest User Restriction

Steps:

- Login as guest user

- Add PayPal payment method

- Attempt to set as default

Expected: Error message displayed, action blocked

QA-4: Expired Payment Restriction

Steps:

- Have an expired PayPal payment method in wallet

- Attempt to set as default

Expected: Error message about expired payment method, action blocked

QA-5: API Testing (Postman/Swagger)

Steps:

- Call SetDefaultWalletOption API with PayPal wallet option ID

- Call GetCustomerWallet API

- Verify response shows PayPal with IsDefault = true

- Call SetDefaultWalletOption API with Apple Pay wallet option ID

- Call GetCustomerWallet API

- Verify response shows Apple Pay with IsDefault = true, PayPal with IsDefault = false

Expected: API responses consistent with expectations

QA-6: Scheduled Payment Renewal

Steps:

- Create subscription with scheduled renewal

- Set Apple Pay as default

- Wait for or trigger renewal

- Check transaction records

Expected: Renewal charges to Apple Pay successfully

QA-7: Switch Default Multiple Times

Steps:

- Set Credit Card as default

- Set PayPal as default

- Set Apple Pay as default

- Set Credit Card as default again

- After each change, verify via API and UI

Expected: Each switch works correctly, previous default is unset

Regression Testing

Areas to Regression Test:

- Credit card as default still works (existing functionality)

- Gift card wallet behavior unchanged

- Account balance wallet behavior unchanged

- Payment without default specified still prompts for payment selection

- All existing reservation flows with explicit payment method selection

Performance Testing

Tests to Run:

- Load test: 1000 concurrent SetDefaultWalletOption calls

- Response time should be < 500ms for 95th percentile

- Database connection pool handles load

- No deadlocks when updating default payment methods concurrently

  • Ensure the IsDefault flag works consistently across all payment types

  • Database operations should be payment-type agnostic

9. Cross-Cutting Concerns to Review

Default Payment Retrieval:

  • Anywhere the system fetches "the default payment method" to use automatically

  • Ensure no code assumes the default will always be a credit card type

Payment Type Validation:

  • Look for validation logic that checks payment types

  • Ensure none inadvertently block PayPal or Apple Pay from being defaults

Method Naming:

  • Methods with names like "SetCreditCardAsPrimary" should either be renamed or verified to handle all payment types

Error Handling:

  • Ensure error messages make sense for all payment types

  • No error messages that say "credit card" when they mean "payment method"

Testing Notes

Unit Tests Required

Test Suite 1: Wallet Service Validation

Location: Internal Services/GolfNow.Services.Wallet/GolfNow.Services.Wallet.UnitTests/

Tests to Add:

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_PayPalDirect_Success
  - Arrange: Customer with active PayPal payment option
  - Act: Call SetDefaultWalletOption with PayPal wallet option ID
  - Assert: Returns true, no exception thrown

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_ApplePay_Success
  - Arrange: Customer with active Apple Pay payment option
  - Act: Call SetDefaultWalletOption with Apple Pay wallet option ID
  - Assert: Returns true, no exception thrown

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_ExpiredPayPal_Fails
  - Arrange: Customer with expired PayPal payment option
  - Act: Call SetDefaultWalletOption with expired PayPal ID
  - Assert: Throws WalletInvalidDataException with appropriate message

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_GuestWallet_PayPal_Fails
  - Arrange: Guest wallet with PayPal payment option
  - Act: Call SetDefaultWalletOption
  - Assert: Throws exception about guest wallets

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_SwitchFromCreditCardToPayPal
  - Arrange: Customer with credit card as default
  - Act: Set PayPal as default
  - Assert: Credit card IsDefault = false, PayPal IsDefault = true

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_SwitchFromPayPalToApplePay
  - Arrange: Customer with PayPal as default
  - Act: Set Apple Pay as default
  - Assert: PayPal IsDefault = false, Apple Pay IsDefault = true

Test Suite 2: Customer Service Integration

Location: Internal Services/GolfNow.Services.Customer/GolfNow.Services.Customer.UnitTests/

Tests to Add:

Test_SetDefaultPaymentOption_PayPal_IntegrationSuccess
Test_SetDefaultPaymentOption_ApplePay_IntegrationSuccess
Test_GetCustomerWallet_DefaultPayPalMarkedCorrectly
Test_GetCustomerWallet_DefaultApplePayMarkedCorrectly

Integration Tests Required

Test Scenario 1: Full Reservation Flow with Default PayPal

Setup:

  1. Create test customer with PayPal payment method

  2. Set PayPal as default via API

  3. Create reservation without specifying payment method

Expected Results:

  • Reservation created successfully

  • Payment charged to PayPal account

  • Reservation payment_method_type = 16 (PayPal Direct)

  • Charge record shows PayPal wallet option ID

Test Scenario 2: Full Reservation Flow with Default Apple Pay

Setup:

  1. Create test customer with Apple Pay payment method

  2. Set Apple Pay as default via API

  3. Create reservation without specifying payment method

Expected Results:

  • Reservation created successfully

  • Payment charged to Apple Pay account

  • Reservation payment_method_type = 17 (Apple Pay)

  • Charge record shows Apple Pay wallet option ID

Test Scenario 3: Scheduled Payment Execution

Setup:

  1. Create customer with scheduled payment

  2. Customer has PayPal as default payment method

  3. Trigger scheduled payment execution

Expected Results:

  • Scheduled payment charges PayPal account

  • Transaction records show PayPal as payment method

  • No errors logged

Test Scenario 4: Refund to PayPal Default

Setup:

  1. Complete reservation with default PayPal

  2. Process full refund

Expected Results:

  • Refund processes successfully

  • Refund goes to original PayPal account

  • Refund status updated correctly

Test Scenario 5: No-Show Charge

Setup:

  1. Create reservation with default Apple Pay

  2. Mark reservation as no-show

  3. Process no-show charge

Expected Results:

  • No-show charge processes to Apple Pay account

  • Charge successful

  • Reservation status updated

Test Scenario 6: Multi-Currency Support

Setup:

  1. Set PayPal as default for customer in USD market

  2. Set PayPal as default for customer in CAD market

  3. Make reservations in both currencies

Expected Results:

  • Both process successfully with correct currency

Manual QA Test Cases

QA-1: Basic Set Default Functionality

Steps:

  1. Login as customer with multiple payment methods (CC, PayPal, Apple Pay)

  2. Navigate to payment methods page

  3. Set PayPal as default

  4. Refresh page

  5. Verify PayPal shows as default

  6. Set Apple Pay as default

  7. Verify only Apple Pay shows as default

Expected: UI correctly shows default indicator, only one method is default at a time

QA-2: Reservation Without Specifying Payment

Steps:

  1. Set PayPal as default payment method

  2. Start new reservation booking

  3. Proceed to payment WITHOUT selecting a payment method

  4. Complete booking

Expected: Booking uses PayPal by default, confirmation shows PayPal

QA-3: Guest User Restriction

Steps:

  1. Login as guest user

  2. Add PayPal payment method

  3. Attempt to set as default

Expected: Error message displayed, action blocked

QA-4: Expired Payment Restriction

Steps:

  1. Have an expired PayPal payment method in wallet

  2. Attempt to set as default

Expected: Error message about expired payment method, action blocked

QA-5: API Testing (Postman/Swagger)

Steps:

  1. Call SetDefaultWalletOption API with PayPal wallet option ID

  2. Call GetCustomerWallet API

  3. Verify response shows PayPal with IsDefault = true

  4. Call SetDefaultWalletOption API with Apple Pay wallet option ID

  5. Call GetCustomerWallet API

  6. Verify response shows Apple Pay with IsDefault = true, PayPal with IsDefault = false

Expected: API responses consistent with expectations

QA-6: Scheduled Payment Renewal

Steps:

  1. Create subscription with scheduled renewal

  2. Set Apple Pay as default

  3. Wait for or trigger renewal

  4. Check transaction records

Expected: Renewal charges to Apple Pay successfully

QA-7: Switch Default Multiple Times

Steps:

  1. Set Credit Card as default

  2. Set PayPal as default

  3. Set Apple Pay as default

  4. Set Credit Card as default again

  5. After each change, verify via API and UI

Expected: Each switch works correctly, previous default is unset

Regression Testing

Areas to Regression Test:

  • Credit card as default still works (existing functionality)

  • Gift card wallet behavior unchanged

  • Account balance wallet behavior unchanged

  • Payment without default specified still prompts for payment selection

  • All existing reservation flows with explicit payment method selection

Performance Testing

Tests to Run:

  • Load test: 1000 concurrent SetDefaultWalletOption calls

  • Response time should be < 500ms for 95th percentile

  • Database connection pool handles load

  • No deadlocks when updating default payment methods concurrently

issues.summary: SPIKE: Check all use cases of Marketing API comparing to GN Pro / RTS
issues.description:
Following analysis in https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/GNI-281, additional effort is required to produce implementation tickets.

Requirements

- Document and clarify the requirements for aligning cart toggle behavior across all booking channels, specifically comparing MarketingAPI (GNC/BRS) and G1/RTS flows.

- In the spike, enumerate all use cases and edge cases for cart toggles and cart allocation, referencing the findings and product notes from GNI-281.

- Identify and involve relevant stakeholders from GNC, BRS, and any downstream systems that may be impacted by changes to cart logic or API payloads.

- Assess the feasibility and impact of the two main options:

- Option A: Keep the current cap of 2 carts per tee time and update UI/messaging to clarify shared cart logic.

- Option B: Update MarketingAPI and downstream systems to allow up to 4 carts per booking, aligning with RTS behavior.

- Document technical dependencies, required code changes, and risks for each option.

- Once analysis is complete, break out implementation tickets for each affected system.

comments.author: Sam Brownlee
comments.body:
Thanks @Andrew Lounsberry , this is really helpful.

The CORE payload and the TransportationTypeId logic give us what we need on the MarketingAPI → CORE → BRS side for “cart included” bookings.

For the rest of the spike we still need to line this up against the GN Pro/RTS behavior, so the missing pieces are:

- An example RTS / GN Pro booking request and payload showing how carts are represented.

- Confirmation of any per‑tee‑time cart caps and where those are enforced (CORE config vs application logic).

Once we have that, we can complete the comparison and outline changes for Option A (stay at 2 carts, clarify messaging) vs Option B (support up to 4 carts in MarketingAPI and downstream).

---
In terms of the requirements of the Spike, I believe the following summarises current position:

- “Aligning cart toggle behavior across all booking channels, specifically comparing MarketingAPI (GNC/BRS) and G1/RTS flows.”

- CORE data only shows one side of the picture:

- CORE → BRS payload for a MarketingAPI booking.

- CORE’s internal “cart included” calculation.

- Still need:

- The equivalent RTS / GN Pro request + payload (what fields they send to CORE, or how they pass carts).

- Any front‑end toggles (per player vs per booking) and what they map to (e.g. TransportationTypeId, a separate “buggies” count, some flag).

- “Enumerate all use cases and edge cases for cart toggles and cart allocation.”

- The CORE snippet helps for “TransportationTypeId = Cart Included” use cases.

- Still need behaviour for:

- “Cart optional” / “cart as an add‑on”.

- Bookings with mixed players (some with carts, some walking).

- Modifications/cancellations and what happens to cart counts.

- Multi‑tee / multi‑round / 9 vs 18 holes.

- Cap logic (e.g. 2 carts per tee time vs more).

- “Assess the feasibility and impact of Option A vs Option B.”

- Can now see one key technical detail:

- There’s no explicit cart count field being passed in this example; it’s derived by CORE.

- To compare options properly still need:

- How RTS/GN Pro represents carts today.

- Whether MarketingAPI already has any way to send explicit cart counts or additional flags.

- Any club configuration for maximum carts per tee time (and where it lives).

- “Document dependencies / code changes / risks per option.”

- Snippet is a good starting point for the CORE dependency and one piece of BRS behavior.

- Still need:

- RTS/GN Pro contracts.

- Any MarketingAPI contracts (e.g., public API models).

- Downstream consumers (e.g., reporting, payouts, cart inventory controls).

---
Next Actions

- Document current MarketingAPI/CORE/BRS behavior:

- For TransportationTypeId = 1:

- Carts allocated as ceil(players / 2).

- Example: 1–2 players → 1 cart, 3–4 players → 2 carts.

- CORE derives cart count, not GN.

- Identify edge cases to verify:

- Other TransportationTypeId values (cart optional / walking only).

- Bookings where GN UI offers a “cart” toggle but no TransportationTypeId is set.

- Modifications where player count changes after initial booking.

- RTS / GN Pro examples

- One or two RTS/GN Pro booking examples (request → CORE payload) where:

- Cart included.

- Cart optional / per‑player selection.

- Any existing documentation for cart handling in RTS/GN Pro.

@Pierce McGeough @David Frame Please review assumptions and update for accuracy.

comments.body:
@Sam Brownlee@David Frame  @Andrew Lounsberry @Desimo Recaido @Joshua Marquess

Without any extra analysis, a simple fix we can try is allowing up to four buggies for the request from core. The only issue is that it most likely will not map each buggy specifically to a player but fill the buggies in 1 to 4

If the booking happened like this

p1: buggy
p2: no buggy
p3: buggy
p4: buggy

It would most likely be represented in the teesheet as the following:

p1: buggy
p2: buggy
p3: buggy
p4: no buggy

Further analysis would be needed to see what would need to happen for a direct player to buggy map. We cannot just swap out and use the RTS endpoints, which already implement similar mapping, as there are other pieces of logic which the Marketing API will be taking care of.

issues.summary: Green fee totals incorrect on ChatGPT App
issues.description:
For facilities not configured for fee messaging, we are displaying a message that the rate includes 3.49 in fees. This is not accurate. The green fee is $29.99 and the fee is $3.49.

We have two options:

- Recommended - If FeeMessagingDisplayRates is NULL, hide the “Includes $$$ in fees text” and use the green fee as the display

- This will match GN logic

- Do UI math to add the the fee amount to the green fee amount and keep the fee message

---
For facilities configured for legal fee messaging (CA,NY, VA, etc), Hot Deals look to be miscalculated

"FeeMessagingDisplayRates": {
"GreensFees": 32.9900,
"TotalPrice": 36.4800,
"TransactionFeesTotal": 3.4900
},

- We need to use the FeeMessagingDisplayRates for both Course and Trade times when FeeMessagingDisplayRates is not null

issues.summary: Support GolfPass Cancellations
issues.description:
In order to meet compliance for price increased products, we will need to expose a subscription cancellation option in the Membership Settings page. This cancellation option will be conditional based on some API attributes.

- Design: https://www.figma.com/design/n4GhZL6oXgfk93DFUhn98h/Cancel-membership-button?node-id=373-19485&m=dev

- We need to make a copy change that is different from the design

- Current: Cancel your GolfPass+ Membership subscription immediately and get a full refund for the renewal period.

- Change to: Cancel your GolfPass+ Membership subscription immediately and get a full refund for the subscription period.

- APIs

- Eligibility API - GET {{prod-api-base-url}}/GolfNowAPI.svc/rest/channel/{{ChannelId}}/customers/{{EmailAddress}}/subscriptions?productTypeId=9

- Target Field: IsEligibleForCancellation

- Cancel/Refund API: POST {{prod-api-base-url}}/GolfNowAPI.svc/rest/channel/{{ChannelId}}/customers/{{EmailAddress}}/subscriptions/{{CustomerSubscriptionId}}/cancelWithRefund

- CustomerSubscriptionId is found in the first endpoint

- Request Body:

{
"CancellationReasonId": 1,
"CancelEvenIfBenefitsUsed": true,
"RefundType": 1,
"SystemUserId": 1
}

issues.summary: Timelyst - QA testing
issues.description:
Overview

End-to-end QA testing of the Timelyst Inventory & Booking application. Many recent tickets involve foundational changes (refactoring, data schema migrations, architectural improvements) that are not individually QA-testable. Since Timelyst has no production traffic yet, this ticket consolidates full-stack validation into a single QA effort covering data sync, facility discovery, and booking workflows.

Environments:

- Timelyst API (Dev): https://timelyst.dev.golfnow.io

- Timelyst API (Stg): https://timelyst.stg.golfnow.io

- Hangfire Dashboard (Dev): timelyst-hangfire-dev.golfnowdmz.local/hangfire/recurring (accessible via AWS Workspace)

- Hangfire Dashboard (Stg): timelyst-hangfire-stg.golfnowdmz.local/hangfire/recurring (accessible via AWS Workspace)

- API Docs: Swagger / Scalar available at the API base URL

---
Test Steps

Step 1 — Configure Interface in CRM

- In the CRM database, create (or verify) an interface configuration for a golf course with a USC and/or CCH provider.

- Ensure the InterfaceAttribute collection has the correct API URL and credentials for the chosen provider(s).

- Note: CCH credentials are stored in the MongoDB InterfaceAttribute collection (synced from CRM via InterfaceAttributeSyncJob), NOT in GCCourseCode.

Step 2 — Wait for CRM → MongoDB Data Sync

- Wait approximately 1 hour for the recurring Hangfire jobs to auto-sync data from the CRM database to the MongoDB Timelyst database.

- Monitor sync progress on the Hangfire recurring jobs dashboard:
http://timelyst-hangfire-dev.golfnowdmz.local/hangfire/recurring

- Verify that Facility, Offering, Service, and InterfaceAttribute data has been synced into MongoDB.

NOTE: Full-sync jobs will attempt to fetch the full CRM table and sync into Mongo, which should be used for initialization. Incremental-sync jobs will only compare the TimeStamp field with the last sync time and only sync records with the updated TimeStamp field.

Step 3 — Create Interface Configuration via API

Using the Timelyst Management API, create interface configurations for USC and CCH providers (if they don't already exist from the sync).

Action

Method

Endpoint

List existing configs

GET

/api/v1/management/interfaceconfiguration

Create new config

POST

/api/v1/management/interfaceconfiguration

Get config by ID

GET

/api/v1/management/interfaceconfiguration/{id}

Update config

PUT

/api/v1/management/interfaceconfiguration/{id}

Delete config

DELETE

/api/v1/management/interfaceconfiguration/{id}

Validation: Confirm configs are created with correct provider type, facility mapping, and enabled status.

Step 4 — Create Product Verticals & Assign to Offerings

Product verticals classify offerings (e.g., "Golf", "Simulator", "Fitting"). The Value is auto-incremented — no need to pass it in the request body.

4a — Create Product Verticals

Action

Method

Endpoint

List product verticals

GET

/api/v1/management/productvertical

Get by ID

GET

/api/v1/management/productvertical/{id}

Create product vertical

POST

/api/v1/management/productvertical

Update product vertical

PUT

/api/v1/management/productvertical/{id}

Delete product vertical

DELETE

/api/v1/management/productvertical/{id}

Activate

POST

/api/v1/management/productvertical/{id}/activate

Deactivate

POST

/api/v1/management/productvertical/{id}/deactivate

Create request body: { "name": "Simulator" } (Value auto-assigned as max + 1)

Validation:

- Confirm Value is auto-incremented (1, 2, 3, ...)

- Confirm Name must be unique

- Confirm Value is immutable after creation (not editable via update)

4b — Assign Product Vertical to Offering

Assigns a product vertical to an existing offering using the ProductVertical's integer Value and the Offering's CRM GolfCourseID.

Action

Method

Endpoint

Assign to offering

POST

/api/v1/management/productvertical/{value}/assign/{offeringCrmId}

Example: POST /api/v1/management/productvertical/1/assign/12951

Validation:

- Confirm the response returns the updated OfferingDto with productVerticalType set

- Confirm assigning an inactive product vertical returns 400

- Confirm non-existent Value or CRM ID returns 404

- Verify the offering in MongoDB shows updated ProductVerticalType field

Step 5 — Create Service Categories & Assign to Services

Service categories use a power-of-2 bitmask pattern (CategoryId = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16...) to support multi-category assignment on services. Create categories first, then assign them to services synced in Step 2.

5a — Create Service Categories

Action

Method

Endpoint

List categories

GET

/api/v1/management/servicecategory

Get category by ID

GET

/api/v1/management/servicecategory/{id}

Create category

POST

/api/v1/management/servicecategory

Delete category

DELETE

/api/v1/management/servicecategory/{id}

Activate category

POST

/api/v1/management/servicecategory/{id}/activate

Deactivate category

POST

/api/v1/management/servicecategory/{id}/deactivate

Example: Create categories like "FullBag" (CategoryId=1), "Irons" (CategoryId=2), "Putter" (CategoryId=4).

Validation:

- Confirm CategoryId must be a unique power of 2

- Confirm Name must be unique

- Confirm categories cannot be modified after creation (immutable — only activate/deactivate/delete)

5b — Assign Categories to Services

Action

Method

Endpoint

Assign categories

POST

/api/v1/management/service/{id}/categories

Request body: { "serviceCategoryIds": [1, 2] }

Multiple categories are combined via OR bitmask (e.g., assigning IDs 1 & 2 sets CategoryId = 3, Category = "FullBag & Irons").

Validation:

- Confirm the service response shows the combined categoryId bitmask and concatenated category name

- Passing an empty array clears category assignments

- Verify assigned categories persist by re-fetching the service via GET /api/v1/management/service/{id}

Step 6 — Bootstrap & Run Reconciliation Jobs

- Trigger the cm-interface-config-bootstrap job in the Hangfire recurring jobs dashboard and refresh the page.

- Verify that two new recurring jobs are created: cm-recon-cch and cm-recon-usc.

- Run each cm-recon-* job. This should create facility-specific jobs following the pattern: cm-usc-f{facilityId}-c{courseId}-d{day}-{sequence} (e.g., cm-usc-f2134-c12951-d0-1).

- These jobs are only created if the CRM golf course is configured with the corresponding interface provider.

- Manually trigger these facility-specific jobs to sync inventory data with the upstream provider (Club Champion or USchedule).

- Verify that after the jobs complete, resource availability data is populated in MongoDB.

Step 7 — Rebuild Discovery Documents & Verify ServiceCategory in Search

After categories are assigned (Step 5) and inventory is synced (Step 6), trigger the Hangfire job that rebuilds the FacilityDiscovery documents so that category data is indexed for search.

- Trigger the facility-discovery-rebuild job (or equivalent) from the Hangfire dashboard.

- Verify the FacilityDiscovery documents in MongoDB contain ServiceCategoryIds arrays on the service entries:

- Each service should list the decomposed power-of-2 category IDs (e.g., bitmask 7 → [1, 2, 4])

- Test search with serviceCategoryIds filter:

#

Action

Method

Endpoint

Key Validations

1

Search by category

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/search?serviceCategoryIds={id}

Only facilities with services matching the category are returned

2

Search by multiple categories

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/search?serviceCategoryIds={id1}&serviceCategoryIds={id2}

Facilities with services matching ANY of the provided categories are returned

3

Detail search by category

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/search/detail?serviceCategoryIds={id}

Full search with services filtered to matching categories; verify serviceCategoryIds array in response

4

Search without filter

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/search

All facilities returned regardless of category

Validation:

- Services in the response include serviceCategoryIds arrays with correct decomposed values

- Filtering by a category that no service has returns zero results

- The category string field on services shows the human-readable concatenated name

Step 8 — Test Client API (Facility Discovery)

Test the 5 client-facing facility discovery endpoints and validate responses.

#

Action

Method

Endpoint

Key Validations

1

Search facilities

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/search

Returns facilities matching search/geo criteria; check latitude, longitude, productVerticalType filters

2

Get facility summary

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/facilities/{facilityId}/summary

Returns basic facility info (amenities, operating hours, timezone); no offerings/services

3

Get facility detail

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/facilities/{facilityId}/detail

Returns full hierarchy (offerings → services); no date-specific availability

4

Get facility availability

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/facilities/{facilityId}/availability?date={yyyyMMdd}

Returns services with availability calendar for the specified date; verify timeslots are present

5

Search with detail

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/search/detail

Full search with services, rate sets, and timeslots; validate pricing and availability

Validation: Confirm that facilities synced in Steps 2–6 appear in search results with correct offerings, services, and availability data.

Step 9 — Test Booking & Cancellation

#

Action

Method

Endpoint

Key Validations

1

Get supported providers

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/management/booking/providers

Returns list of supported providers (USC, CCH)

2

Make a reservation

POST

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/management/booking/reserve?provider={USC\|CCH}

Booking succeeds; confirmation number returned

3

Verify booking reflected

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/facilities/{facilityId}/availability?date={yyyyMMdd}

The booked timeslot shows as unavailable / reduced capacity

4

Cancel the reservation

POST

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/management/booking/cancel?provider={USC\|CCH}

Cancellation succeeds using confirmation number

5

Verify cancellation reflected

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/facilities/{facilityId}/availability?date={yyyyMMdd}

The previously booked timeslot is available again

Validation: After booking, the availability endpoint should reflect the consumed timeslot. After cancellation, the timeslot should be restored.

---
Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] CRM → MongoDB data sync completes successfully via Hangfire jobs

- [ ] Interface configurations can be created/read/updated/deleted via the Management API

- [ ] Product verticals can be created (with auto-incremented Value), listed, updated, activated, deactivated, and deleted

- [ ] Product verticals can be assigned to offerings via the assign endpoint using Value and CRM ID

- [ ] Service categories can be created, listed, activated, deactivated, and deleted

- [ ] Service categories can be assigned to services and the bitmask/name is correctly computed

- [ ] Bootstrap job creates the expected reconciliation jobs (cm-recon-cch, cm-recon-usc)

- [ ] Reconciliation jobs create facility-specific sync jobs and successfully sync upstream provider data

- [ ] FacilityDiscovery documents contain ServiceCategoryIds after rebuild

- [ ] Search endpoints correctly filter by serviceCategoryIds query parameter

- [ ] All 5 client facility discovery endpoints return correct data including category information

- [ ] Booking endpoint successfully creates a reservation and timeslot availability is updated

- [ ] Cancellation endpoint successfully cancels a reservation and timeslot availability is restored

/api/v1/management/service/{id}/categories

Request body: { "serviceCategoryIds": [1, 2] }

Multiple categories are combined via OR bitmask (e.g., assigning IDs 1 & 2 sets CategoryId = 3, Category = "FullBag & Irons").

Validation:

  • Confirm the service response shows the combined categoryId bitmask and concatenated category name

  • Passing an empty array clears category assignments

  • Verify assigned categories persist by re-fetching the service via GET /api/v1/management/service/{id}

Step 6 — Bootstrap & Run Reconciliation Jobs

  1. Trigger the cm-interface-config-bootstrap job in the Hangfire recurring jobs dashboard and refresh the page.

  2. Verify that two new recurring jobs are created: cm-recon-cch and cm-recon-usc.

  3. Run each cm-recon-* job. This should create facility-specific jobs following the pattern: cm-usc-f{facilityId}-c{courseId}-d{day}-{sequence} (e.g., cm-usc-f2134-c12951-d0-1).

    • These jobs are only created if the CRM golf course is configured with the corresponding interface provider.

  4. Manually trigger these facility-specific jobs to sync inventory data with the upstream provider (Club Champion or USchedule).

  5. Verify that after the jobs complete, resource availability data is populated in MongoDB.

Step 7 — Rebuild Discovery Documents & Verify ServiceCategory in Search

After categories are assigned (Step 5) and inventory is synced (Step 6), trigger the Hangfire job that rebuilds the FacilityDiscovery documents so that category data is indexed for search.

  1. Trigger the facility-discovery-rebuild job (or equivalent) from the Hangfire dashboard.

  2. Verify the FacilityDiscovery documents in MongoDB contain ServiceCategoryIds arrays on the service entries:

    • Each service should list the decomposed power-of-2 category IDs (e.g., bitmask 7 → [1, 2, 4])

  3. Test search with serviceCategoryIds filter:

#

Action

Method

Endpoint

Key Validations

1

Search by category

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/search?serviceCategoryIds={id}

Only facilities with services matching the category are returned

2

Search by multiple categories

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/search?serviceCategoryIds={id1}&serviceCategoryIds={id2}

Facilities with services matching ANY of the provided categories are returned

3

Detail search by category

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/search/detail?serviceCategoryIds={id}

Full search with services filtered to matching categories; verify serviceCategoryIds array in response

4

Search without filter

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/search

All facilities returned regardless of category

Validation:

  • Services in the response include serviceCategoryIds arrays with correct decomposed values

  • Filtering by a category that no service has returns zero results

  • The category string field on services shows the human-readable concatenated name

Step 8 — Test Client API (Facility Discovery)

Test the 5 client-facing facility discovery endpoints and validate responses.

#

Action

Method

Endpoint

Key Validations

1

Search facilities

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/search

Returns facilities matching search/geo criteria; check latitude, longitude, productVerticalType filters

2

Get facility summary

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/facilities/{facilityId}/summary

Returns basic facility info (amenities, operating hours, timezone); no offerings/services

3

Get facility detail

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/facilities/{facilityId}/detail

Returns full hierarchy (offerings → services); no date-specific availability

4

Get facility availability

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/facilities/{facilityId}/availability?date={yyyyMMdd}

Returns services with availability calendar for the specified date; verify timeslots are present

5

Search with detail

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/search/detail

Full search with services, rate sets, and timeslots; validate pricing and availability

Validation: Confirm that facilities synced in Steps 2–6 appear in search results with correct offerings, services, and availability data.

Step 9 — Test Booking & Cancellation

#

Action

Method

Endpoint

Key Validations

1

Get supported providers

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/management/booking/providers

Returns list of supported providers (USC, CCH)

2

Make a reservation

POST

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/management/booking/reserve?provider={USC\|CCH}

Booking succeeds; confirmation number returned

3

Verify booking reflected

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/facilities/{facilityId}/availability?date={yyyyMMdd}

The booked timeslot shows as unavailable / reduced capacity

4

Cancel the reservation

POST

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/management/booking/cancel?provider={USC\|CCH}

Cancellation succeeds using confirmation number

5

Verify cancellation reflected

GET

/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/client/facilitydiscovery/facilities/{facilityId}/availability?date={yyyyMMdd}

The previously booked timeslot is available again

Validation: After booking, the availability endpoint should reflect the consumed timeslot. After cancellation, the timeslot should be restored.

Acceptance Criteria

  • [ ] CRM → MongoDB data sync completes successfully via Hangfire jobs

  • [ ] Interface configurations can be created/read/updated/deleted via the Management API

  • [ ] Product verticals can be created (with auto-incremented Value), listed, updated, activated, deactivated, and deleted

  • [ ] Product verticals can be assigned to offerings via the assign endpoint using Value and CRM ID

  • [ ] Service categories can be created, listed, activated, deactivated, and deleted

  • [ ] Service categories can be assigned to services and the bitmask/name is correctly computed

  • [ ] Bootstrap job creates the expected reconciliation jobs (cm-recon-cch, cm-recon-usc)

  • [ ] Reconciliation jobs create facility-specific sync jobs and successfully sync upstream provider data

  • [ ] FacilityDiscovery documents contain ServiceCategoryIds after rebuild

  • [ ] Search endpoints correctly filter by serviceCategoryIds query parameter

  • [ ] All 5 client facility discovery endpoints return correct data including category information

  • [ ] Booking endpoint successfully creates a reservation and timeslot availability is updated

  • [ ] Cancellation endpoint successfully cancels a reservation and timeslot availability is restored

New: Product Vertical Management & Assignment (PR #84)

Two new capabilities have been added that should be tested between Steps 3 and 4:

Create Product Verticals

Product verticals classify offerings (e.g., "Golf", "Simulator", "Fitting"). The Value is now auto-incremented — no need to pass it in the request body.

Action

Method

Endpoint

List product verticals

GET

/api/v1/management/productvertical

Get by ID

GET

/api/v1/management/productvertical/{id}

Create product vertical

POST

/api/v1/management/productvertical

Update product vertical

PUT

/api/v1/management/productvertical/{id}

Delete product vertical

DELETE

/api/v1/management/productvertical/{id}

Activate

POST

/api/v1/management/productvertical/{id}/activate

Deactivate

POST

/api/v1/management/productvertical/{id}/deactivate

Create request body: { "name": "Simulator" } (Value auto-assigned as max + 1)

Validation:

- Confirm Value is auto-incremented (1, 2, 3, ...)

- Confirm Name must be unique

- Confirm Value is immutable after creation (not editable via update)

Assign Product Vertical to Offering

Assigns a product vertical to an existing offering using the ProductVertical's integer Value and the Offering's CRM GolfCourseID.

Action

Method

Endpoint

Assign to offering

POST

/api/v1/management/productvertical/{value}/assign/{offeringCrmId}

Example: POST /api/v1/management/productvertical/1/assign/12951

Validation:

- Confirm the response returns the updated OfferingDto with productVerticalType set

- Confirm assigning an inactive product vertical returns 400

- Confirm non-existent Value or CRM ID returns 404

- Verify the offering in MongoDB shows updated ProductVerticalType field

PR: https://github.com/GolfNowEng/gn-svc-timelyst/pull/84

issues.summary: SmartPlay Featured Products | Featured product icon is missing from reservations
issues.description:
Location: Greenfield Lakes GC

Issue:

The course partner is reporting that the featured product icon is missing from reservations on their tee sheet.

Order 100491876486 - Reservation on 1-APR-2026 at 10:07am (2 hours difference is tracked in GN1S-7822)

We can see that there is no icon associated with the reservation on the tee sheet.

If we look at our external KB documentation in https://golfnow.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/Knowledge__kav/ka0WQ000000MBZVYA4/view, we can see that we should be expecting a featured product icon to show up that indicates this tee time involves a featured product purchase.

Reproduced: Yes (it affects all reservations at az_greenfieldlakesgc (EZRTS) /nc_rockyriver (BRS) with Featured Products)

Steps to Reproduce:

- For any online reservation at az_greenfieldlakesgc/nc_rockyriver that involves a featured product purchase, bring up the date/time on the tee sheet

Expected Behavior:

- Featured product icon shows on the reservation to indicate a featured product purchase was made.

Actual Behavior:

- There is no indication that a featured product purchase was made that is associated with this reservation.

Workaround:

- None

issues.summary: FeeConfiguration - Create Columns for GP Waivability and Refundability
issues.description:
Goal

Add explicit FeeConfiguration support for GolfPass waived-fee-credit waivability and refundability so each configured fee can independently define whether it can be waived by a GolfPass waived fee credit and whether it is refundable during cancellation/refund flows.

This is a foundational data/model ticket for the Customizable Transaction Fees epic. It should not attempt to build the full multi-fee framework, GNC UI revamp, fee messaging changes, tax handling, or revenue allocation behavior.

---
Background

The Customizable Transaction Fees epic requires different fee types to behave differently. For example:

- The standard GolfNow transaction/convenience fee may be waivable with a GolfPass waived fee credit.

- A tourism, city, county, or other regulatory fee may need to be non-waivable.

- Some fees may be refundable.

- Some fees may be non-refundable.

Goal

Add explicit FeeConfiguration support for GolfPass waived-fee-credit waivability and refundability so each configured fee can independently define whether it can be waived by a GolfPass waived fee credit and whether it is refundable during cancellation/refund flows.

This is a foundational data/model ticket for the Customizable Transaction Fees epic. It should not attempt to build the full multi-fee framework, GNC UI revamp, fee messaging changes, tax handling, or revenue allocation behavior.

Background

The Customizable Transaction Fees epic requires different fee types to behave differently. For example:

  • The standard GolfNow transaction/convenience fee may be waivable with a GolfPass waived fee credit.

  • A tourism, city, county, or other regulatory fee may need to be non-waivable.

  • Some fees may be refundable.

  • Some fees may be non-refundable.

Today, FeeConfiguration does not have clear per-fee fields that let downstream systems determine these behaviors from configuration. We need to add those fields first so future tickets can safely apply waiver and refund behavior without hard-coding fee categories.

Scope

Add new fields to the FeeConfiguration data model to support per-fee behavior:

  • GolfPass waivable flag

    • Indicates whether this fee can be waived by a GolfPass waived-fee-credit benefit.

    • Example values: true for standard GolfNow transaction fee, false for tourism/city/county fees.

  • Refundable flag

    • Indicates whether this fee is refundable when a reservation is cancelled/refunded.

    • Example values: true for refundable convenience fees, false for non-refundable tourism/city/county fees.

Implementation should include the appropriate database/schema changes and any required data access/model/DTO updates so these values can be read by downstream API, Reservation Service, and future GNC configuration work.

Defaults / Backward Compatibility

Existing production behavior must remain unchanged after the columns are added.

Default values for existing FeeConfiguration records should preserve current behavior (current behavior is that all fees and waivable and refundable).

Acceptance Criteria

  1. FeeConfiguration schema supports a per-fee GolfPass waivable field.

  2. FeeConfiguration schema supports a per-fee refundable field.

  3. Existing FeeConfiguration records are backfilled/defaulted so current production behavior is preserved.

  4. The new fields can be read wherever FeeConfiguration data is retrieved for API/Reservation Service use.

issues.summary: [Commerce] Facility Closure / Update casing Tee Times to Fail in the Add to Cart process
issues.description:
When adding Tee Times to cart when the course has an update (such as reducing to 9 holes from 18 holes) it fails with an error message stating the Tee Time could not be found. Root cause is that the store procedure that gets the tee times only filters facilities if they have an active closure. This needs to be updated so it also looks at if Disable

Inventory is true and allow facilities that are active but don’t have disable inventory set to true.

issues.summary: [TO] LEGACY - Support GolfPass Cancellations
issues.description:
In order to meet compliance for price increased products, we will need to expose a subscription cancellation option in the Membership Settings page. This cancellation option will be conditional based on some API attributes. This applies to the GN Membership Settings as well as the GolfPass White Label Membership Settings.

- Design: https://www.figma.com/design/n4GhZL6oXgfk93DFUhn98h/Cancel-membership-button?node-id=246-46405&m=dev#1745521556

- APIs

- Eligibility API - GET {{prod-api-base-url}}/GolfNowAPI.svc/rest/channel/{{ChannelId}}/customers/{{EmailAddress}}/subscriptions?productTypeId=9

- Target Field: IsEligibleForCancellation

- Cancel/Refund API: POST {{prod-api-base-url}}/GolfNowAPI.svc/rest/channel/{{ChannelId}}/customers/{{EmailAddress}}/subscriptions/{{CustomerSubscriptionId}}/cancelWithRefund

- CustomerSubscriptionId is found in the first endpoint

- Request Body:

{
"CancellationReasonId": 1,
"CancelEvenIfBenefitsUsed": true,
"RefundType": 1,
"SystemUserId": 1
}

- Always pass in CancellationReasonId = 1

- This means “Too Expensive”

- Always pass in CancelEvenIfBenefitsUsed = true

- Always Pass in RefundType = 0

- This means “Full Refund”

- Always pass in SystemUserId = 1

- Logic

- If IsEligibleForCancellation = true

- Display the Cancel Subscription option - Passed

- Tapping the button should open a modal with the option to confirm - Passed

- Confirming should submit the Cancel/Refund API above - Passed

- Membership settings should reload the page with the “No active memberships” treatment and we should make sure we resubmit any customer data in the site to make sure they are no longer recognized as a GP Member - Passed

- Remove the GP icons under their name, show the non member version of various pages, etc - Passed

- Currently this page is only accessible for members so a part of this work will be to make this Membership Settings page visible for all users - Passed

- Non members will simply see the no memberships version in the design - Passed

- To display the recently cancelled subscription info, you can add this to the Get Subscription API: &cancelledIncluded=true

- If IsEligibleForCancellation = false

- Do not show the Cancel Subscription option and the page will remain as is - Passed

- For the GolfPass CTA when you are not a member, link to the following product

- GN US/TO Prod: /7129411482949

- QA: /7129410862949 Passed

- GN UK Prod: /4929411702949

- QA: /492946602949

- GN AU Prod: /4529411712949

- QA: /452941462949

- Testing

- Most of the test cases are listed https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/CORE-14272 Passed

- Happy Path - Passed

- Create a user with a State of New York and billing address also in New York

- Buy one of the $119 free trial products

- Renew into the paid $119 product

- The IsEligibleForCancellation should be true as long as today’s date is within 15 days of the renewal date

- The Cancel Option should show

issues.summary: Apple Pay Follow Up Bugs
issues.description:
- Merchant Key Mismatch

- When we try to book a teetime that is for a full stack facility. We are generating the PaymentMethodKey using the chargeBy merchantKey, but at the time of transaction, we are doing it with the fullstack merchantKey that is different than the chargeBy. This is causing issues on payment processing. We should use the merchantKey that we are going to use for the transaction to generate the paymentMethodKey. (This will not required changes from CORE side since Payment processing team is going to fix this on their end)

- Guest support

- Currently guests cannot create wallets. This fails the apple pay flow because we need it stored for No Shows. We need to update guest logic to store a wallet ONLY if it is apple pay

- Credit cards should not create a stored wallet for Guest

- Add authorization to the reservation flow

- This already exists in the subscription flow

(This will not required changes from CORE side since Payment processing team is going to fix this on their end)

  2. Guest support

issues.summary: Use LaunchDarkly for configuration + accept FacilityId and ChannelId inputs
issues.description:
We need to replace the current web.config-based toggling for the FeeConfiguration code with a server-side LaunchDarkly feature flag. The goal is to be able to remotely enable the FeeConfiguration behavior in production for testing without editing web.config or temporarily hard-coding IDs.

This work supports the larger change to move fee messaging to run after final fee totals are composed (https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/CORE-14117#icft=CORE-14117). This ticket focuses only on the feature-flagging and configuration input portion: enable FeeConfiguration through LaunchDarkly.

Acceptance Criteria

- LaunchDarkly flag created

- A server-side LaunchDarkly feature flag is created

- Behavior and fallback

- Default behavior remains legacy (FeeConfiguration disabled) unless the LaunchDarkly flag enables it.

- While migrating, if LaunchDarkly is unreachable for any reason, the code should fall back to the existing CRMConfig value (so production safety is maintained). A separate follow-up can remove the fallback after rollout.

- Operational readiness

- Logging of some sort includes whether FeeConfiguration was enabled by LaunchDarkly and the facilityId/channelId used for evaluation

NOTE: This will connect to both API 2.1 and Reservation Service

Removed the FacilityId/ChannelId context key from this ticket, will consider implementing in a future ticket. - @Daniel McNaughton

TESTED IN AWS STG :

For Trade Hot Deals

TRADE / HOT DEAL :

Validate the overrides for the TransactionFeesTotal in the Response → and TransactionFeesTotal  ,  FeeMessagingDisplayRates is using this to show the total breakdown.

If there are no other fees configured other than the  → OGFOwnerTransactionFee  → From the CRMOwnerGolfFacility table , then that will be displayed on the Fee Messaging Object for TRNFEE

That Value can be Overridden by → the Fee value from the -> Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees table , if it has a value for the facility ( which is controlled by the constrain if the Facility is Master or not ) → and that is provided by the CRMGolfFacility table which tells us that value from the → GFStatus column

The Fee Value from the → Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees table can be Overridden by → Launch Darkly Flag → Based off of the Channel ID

If the Flag is disabled → and there is a value in the Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees table , then that will be shown

If the Flag is Enabled → the value form the Amount Column from the CRM.Revenue.FeeConfiguration table will be displayed

---

We also have the a value in the CRM.Revenue.FeeConfiguration table , but because the Launch Darkly Flag is OFF , we are not seeing that value :

After Turning ON that flag , we should see that value override the TRNFEE amount from the Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees table :

---
COURSE :

→ Not affected by Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees , as they apply to Trade Tee Times

→ When Launch Darkly is ON , the TRNFEE from will be displayed for Course Tee Times :

issues.summary: Support Apple Pay Transactions
issues.description:
Apple Pay supports the ability for multi merchant transactions. We need to update our current Apple Pay logic to support this as well. This will be used for tee time + GolfPass transactions in sidecart. We very likely need to revisit our original apple pay workflow and clean it up.

Apple Pay Docs: https://applepaydemo.apple.com/ , https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/apple-pay , https://developer.apple.com/apple-pay/marketing/ , https://developer.apple.com/apple-pay/sandbox-testing/

- Expose Apple Pay on the UI

- Design: https://www.figma.com/design/mOWXt8yuZAaHEXULT5utOa/Apple-Pay---MVP?node-id=59-117&p=f&m=dev

- When a user attempts to purchase a standalone tee time or standalone golfpass product, submit the single cryptogram to API 2.1

- API: TBD

- When a user attempts to purchase a tee time + golfpass sidecart, submit the cryptograms to API 2.1

- API Logic: TBD

- Create a remote config to enable/disable Apple Pay per app

- Labels in the Apple Pay module

- When we the GolfPass+ line item in this view, we need to label it as Free Trial

- In the invoice response, there is the following object

"ProductPricingTags": {
"IsComplementary": false,
"IsEmployee": false,
"IsMilitary": false,
"IsStudent": false,
"IsTrial": true
},

- If IsTrial=true, label = GolfPass+ Annual Free Trial

- If IsTrial=false, label = GolfPass+ Annual

Dev Testing:

- This should have the same validations as a credit card transaction where GolfPass is processed first

- This should have the same validations as a credit card transaction where if the tee time fails, the GolfPass can still succeed and purchased

- Ensure that standalone tee time (course prepaid and trade) transactions function with all payment methods including Apple Pay

- Ensure that standalone GolfPass transactions function with all payment methods including Apple Pay

- Test with Hot Deals, Course times, Prepaid Course Times, Prepaid times with GN & GC revenue allocation all in combination with and without GolfPass

- Ensure the correct amounts get charged when using points, gift card and account credits

- With and without promo codes

- Test on EUR, GBP, CAD and AUD currency

- This will require full regression of Checkout

Prod TestFlight - Post 4/28 CORE Release

- Keep track and document all ReservationIds and GolfPass subscriptions/customers used to test. We will need these for data/payments validation downstream

- Hot Deal

- Refund a hot deal

- Course time, due at course

- do not cancel

- Wait until the following day and then we will force a renewal in GNC to the paid product

issues.summary: Move Fee-Messaging to Post-Fee-Calculation & Use FeeConfiguration (API 2.1)
issues.description:
The original story proposed adding a new stored procedure + API toggle to decouple fee retrieval from the TeeTime stored procedure. After discussion with @Daniel McNaughton, we will not change stored procedures. Instead we’ll use the FeeConfiguration module in API 2.1 for this work and ensure fee messaging executes only after the final tee-time transaction fee totals are calculated.

The current problem: Fee Messaging (starting at line ~1727 in TeeTimeRepository.cs) executes too early in the pipeline and therefore does not see the final transaction fee totals. When FeeConfiguration is enabled (or when Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees is modified), the early messaging produces incorrect fee messages.

Goal:

- Identify the place(s) in the request pipeline where all fee calculation logic is completed (including FeeConfiguration module behavior and any Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees overrides).

- Move the fee-messaging process to operate on tee-times after that point so messaging always reflects the final, composed transaction fee totals.

- Use the existing FeeConfiguration module in API 2.1 (no stored proc changes). Default legacy behavior must remain unchanged unless FeeConfiguration is enabled.

Affected endpoints / flows (as called out in the original ticket)

- API 2.1 GetTeeTimes

- API 2.1 GetInvoice

- API 2.1 TeeTimeInvoice

- Reservation Service — Invoice flow
(These endpoints must behave consistently after the change.)

---
Example:

- Revenue team updates trade transaction fees at FID 55 from $3.49 to $1.99

- This update is stored in Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees (not CRMOwnerGolfFacility)

- Current outcome: The API returns $3.49 fee messaging and therefore the UI displays this incorrect value

- Expected outcome: The API should return the $1.99 fee messaging in order for front end to display the correct value

Note: The transaction fee is correct at the invoice level, it’s just the Fee Messaging that needs updated

API results:

UI results:

---

Acceptance Criteria

- No stored proc changes. The database stored procedures remain unchanged. Fee retrieval is performed via the FeeConfiguration module in API 2.1 when enabled.

- Fee-messaging runs only after final totals. Fee-messaging logic is moved so it operates on tee-times after the application layer has composed final totals (after FeeConfiguration and any Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees adjustments). Messaging content must match the final totals.

- Behavior parity / safe default. Default behavior (when FeeConfiguration is disabled) remains identical to current production behavior. When FeeConfiguration is enabled, messages reflect fee totals produced by the FeeConfiguration module + any Revenue.DynamicTransactionFees overrides.

- All affected endpoints updated. GetTeeTimes, GetInvoice, TeeTimeInvoice, and Reservation Service invoice flows all produce correct fee messaging across both legacy and FeeConfiguration-enabled modes.

---
Technical Notes / Implementation Guidance

- Investigation phase

- Locate the fee-messaging implementation referenced by Daniel — currently beginning at ~line 1727 in TeeTimeRepository.cs. Review how and when it runs relative to fee composition.

- Identify every place in the code path where transaction fees are finalized/aggregated for the affected endpoints (for example, final composition in application layer or where invoice totals are built). This may be inside TeeTimeRepository post-processing, invoice composition routines, or Reservation Service invoice flow.

- Identify where FeeConfiguration module is invoked for API 2.1 calls (and where FeeConfiguration may alter totals). Confirm how FeeConfiguration combines with Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees.

- Move/Refactor fee-messaging

- Extract/encapsulate the fee-messaging code so it can be invoked after final totals are composed. The new invocation point should be the single canonical location where the final tee-time totals are guaranteed to be complete (i.e., after any FeeConfiguration logic and any dynamic fee overrides).

- Ensure the message builder references the final totals from the in-memory tee-time objects returned to the API layer (not from intermediate values).

- Where multiple flows produce tee-times (GetTeeTimes, GetInvoice, TeeTimeInvoice, Reservation Service), make sure each flow invokes the new post-composition messaging path.

- FeeConfiguration integration

- When FeeConfiguration is enabled, ensure fee-messaging consumes totals that FeeConfiguration produced (API 2.1 module). If FeeConfiguration is disabled, ensure existing legacy totals and messaging are used.

- Ensure that changes in Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees also reflect in the final totals that the message consumes.

issues.summary: Implement Payment Processing Entity Model and Routing System
issues.description:
Overview

Design and implement a payment processing routing system backed by MongoDB Atlas. The system maps a MerchantAccount and CurrencyCode to a set of supported PaymentProcessors with failover routing support, using a pre-computed materialized view to eliminate runtime aggregation.

---
High-Level Requirements

1. Entity Model — MongoDB Collections

MerchantAccount (merchantAccounts)

- Represents a business entity that processes payments

- Fields: legalName, merchantType (enum), merchantReferenceId, legacyReferenceId, profile (embedded subdoc), soft-delete fields (isDeleted/deletedAt)

- Unique indexes on legacyReferenceId and merchantReferenceId (sparse, partial filter on non-deleted)

PaymentProcessor (paymentProcessors)

- Defines a processor, the payment method it handles, required merchant configuration schema, and per-currency settings

- Fields: name, processorKey, status, paymentMethodType, requiredParams[] (with validation patterns and target field), baseParams, baseSecrets (CSFLE encrypted), currencyProfiles[]

- Each requiredParam specifies a target field (configParams or configSecrets) for validation routing

MerchantPaymentProfile (merchantPaymentProfiles)

- Maps a merchant to a specific processor for a given payment method and currency

- Supports failover routing via priority field (0 = primary, 1 = first fallback, etc.)

- Fields: merchantId (FK), paymentMethodType, currencyCode, paymentProcessorId (FK), priority, status, configParams (plain), configSecrets (CSFLE encrypted)

- Compound unique indexes enforce one-processor-per-priority and one-priority-per-processor per merchant/method/currency

2. Materialized View — merchantProcessorRoutes

- Pre-computed join of profiles and processors, rebuilt via Atlas Database Triggers

- Groups by merchantId + paymentMethodType + currencyCode with ordered processors array

- Denormalizes merchantReferenceId and processorKey for direct lookups

- Carries both plaintext params and encrypted secrets (CSFLE passthrough)

- Primary routing query: lookup by merchantId (or merchantReferenceId) + currencyCode

3. Rebuild Pipeline (Atlas Triggers)

- Triggered on changes to merchantPaymentProfiles and paymentProcessors

- Scoped rebuild for affected merchant(s) only

- Pipeline: match non-inactive profiles → sort by priority → $lookup processors (non-inactive, active currency) → $lookup merchant accounts (non-deleted) → group → $merge upsert

- Stale route cleanup: delete route documents with empty processors array post-rebuild

- Scheduled trigger for periodic full rebuild as consistency safety net

4. Encryption — Atlas CSFLE

- All *Secrets fields encrypted via Client-Side Field Level Encryption

- Encryption/decryption in the MongoDB driver (AutoEncryptionSettings)

- KMS provider: AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS (local key for dev)

- Random encryption algorithm (no equality queries needed on secrets)

- Materialized view passes encrypted BinData through; decryption at read time by driver

5. Cross-Cutting Concerns

Soft Deletes

- Entities with status field: Inactive = soft delete, partial filter indexes exclude inactive

- Entities without status (MerchantAccount): explicit isDeleted/deletedAt fields

Config Params vs Secrets Split

- configParams/baseParams: non-sensitive, plaintext, queryable, visible in Atlas UI

- configSecrets/baseSecrets: sensitive, CSFLE encrypted, opaque BinData on server

6. Transaction Routing Context (Capture-Time Snapshot)

- On payment capture, snapshot routing context onto the transaction record

- Snapshot: processorKey, processorId, profileId, configParams (plain), processorTransactionRef

- Enables post-capture operations (refunds, voids) independent of current profile state

- Do NOT snapshot secrets or currencyProfile details

7. Application-Layer Validation

- Cross-document validation of configParams/configSecrets against PaymentProcessor.requiredParams

- Validate plaintext values before encryption

- MongoDB schema validators use bsonType: "binData" for encrypted fields

---
Enums

Enum

Values

MerchantType

GolfFacility, ServiceProvider, Aggregator

PaymentMethodType

GiftCard, CreditCard, AccountBalance, ApplePay, PayPal, etc

Status

Active, Inactive, Pending

---
Reference

Full entity design spec: payment-processing-entity-design.md

issues.summary: Payment Processors (Gift Card, Apple Pay, Funded Coupon) and Execution Layer (specs 028-029)
issues.description:
Context

Specs 028 and 029 deliver the final Phase 1 payment processor implementations and the durable execution layer that orchestrates them.

- Spec 028 (.specify/specs/028-payment-adapters-giftcard-applepay-fundedcoupon/spec.md) defines processor behavior for GolfNow gift card, EZLinks gift card, Apple Pay, and funded coupon tenders — the remaining Phase 1 processors beyond CreditCard (spec 024), Affiliate, and AccountBalance (spec 026b). Builds on route-selected processor resolution (spec 026b) and the tokenization pipeline (spec 027a).

- Spec 029 (.specify/specs/029-payment-execution-journals-idempotency/spec.md) defines the durable execution layer for AUTH, CAPTURE, CREDIT, and VOID actions across all payment processors. Adds the execution coordinator, PaymentAttempt persistence, immutable PaymentActivityJournal and PaymentDecisionJournal entries, ExecutedProcessorContext capture, and idempotency enforcement across saga retries.

These belong together because spec 029 depends on spec 028 processors being in place, and both specs together complete the Phase 1 payment execution surface.

Scope

Spec 028 — Processors

- Gift card processor family (GolfNow + EZLinks) implementing IPaymentProcessor + IBalanceQueryProcessor.

- Real-time gift card balance query via IBalanceQueryProcessor.GetBalanceAsync (non-mutating).

- Apple Pay processor consuming only tokenized/normalized instrument references from spec 027a.

- Funded coupon processor treating funded coupon as PaymentMethodType.FundedCoupon, not an entitlement.

- ProcessorCapabilityDeclaration for all covered processors.

- Error normalization: insufficient balance, expired gift card, invalid coupon, processor unavailable, unsupported action.

- DI registration and route-selected processor resolution per spec 026b.

Spec 029 — Execution Layer

- Payment execution coordinator invoked by checkout and post-purchase sagas.

- PaymentAttempt creation/update (UUIDv7 business id) per action per route group.

- PaymentActivityJournal and PaymentDecisionJournal append rules (immutable, no PCI data).

- Adapter idempotency key generation and replay behavior (same request id → return committed result).

- ExecutedProcessorContext capture for refund/void routing independence.

- Per-action retry and failure classification boundaries.

- Multi-merchant authorization: distinct attempts for one tender split across merchant route groups.

- SCA/customer-action-required pause logic for the attempt chain.

Out of Scope

- CreditCard, Affiliate, and AccountBalance processors.

- Circuit breaker and failover decision policy.

- SCA challenge callback flow (callback handling deferred).

- Funding source accounting policy for coupons.

- New external gift-card service schema.

- Payment journal retention/archival beyond live operational storage.

Acceptance Criteria

Spec 028

- Spec 028 .specify/specs/028-payment-adapters-giftcard-applepay-fundedcoupon/spec.md references this Jira ticket.

- GolfNow and EZLinks gift card processors implement IPaymentProcessor + IBalanceQueryProcessor.

- Apple Pay processor consumes only tokenized/normalized references; unnormalized payloads are rejected before external I/O.

- FundedCouponProcessor treats funded coupon as PaymentMethodType.FundedCoupon and never routes through entitlement providers.

- All processors expose a complete ProcessorCapabilityDeclaration; unsupported actions are rejected by capability checks, not processor exceptions.

- Gift card, Apple Pay, and funded coupon expected business failures return non-throwing ResultWrapper-compatible typed results.

- IBalanceQueryProcessor.GetBalanceAsync returns available balance, currency code, and expiration date for a valid gift card reference without any ledger mutation.

- Gift card balance query failures (expired card, unavailable service, invalid reference) return typed BalanceQueryResult statuses and do not throw.

- IPaymentProcessorRegistry.TryGetBalanceQueryProcessor returns true for all registered gift card PaymentProcessorKey values.

- No processor log path leaks full token, wallet payload, or gift-card secret data (PCI compliance per spec 003).

- Funded coupon appears only in payment tests and never in entitlement provider tests.

Spec 029
12. Spec 029 .specify/specs/029-payment-execution-journals-idempotency/spec.md references this Jira ticket.
13. A payment execution coordinator handles AUTH, CAPTURE, CREDIT, and VOID for all Phase 1 processors.
14. Every payment action creates or updates a PaymentAttempt with a UUIDv7 business id.
15. Every payment action appends an immutable PaymentActivityJournal entry.
16. Every adapter/action selection appends an immutable PaymentDecisionJournal entry including route snapshot identity, AdapterKey, payment method, processor code, action, and reason.

18. Duplicate execution requests with the same request id return the committed result without re-invoking the adapter.
19. Expected payment declines are non-throwing outcomes; infrastructure failures may throw per saga policy.
20. One tender split across two merchants creates two distinct PaymentAttempt records with different merchant/route context and idempotency identities.
21. Refund, capture, and void actions route from original ExecutedProcessorContext.AdapterKey and configuration reference, not a fresh route snapshot.
22. Journal serialization passes PCI-sensitive data analyzer checks (spec 003).
23. A tender is not marked fully authorized until all required route-group authorization attempts for that tender are terminal success.

24. dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.
25. dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

issues.summary: SmartPlay | Online Orders default "Effective Date" search criteria does not return any data when page loads
issues.description:
Location: Greenfield Lakes / Moody Gardens

Issue:

The default effective date in Online Orders does not return any data when the page initially loads, leading the user to believe there are no future online orders.

See example below - page is initially brought up:

However, when we choose “Today” as the effective date, it returns data.

If we change the criteria manually, it also produces results.

Reproduced: Yes (any location that uses online orders/SmartPlay)

Steps to Reproduce:

- On a day where there is an online order with the effective date equal to the current date, go into Orders > Online Orders

Expected Results:

- Online orders effective from the default current date up to one month out are displayed

Actual Results:

- No data is displayed

Workaround:

- Manually change the date criteria to trigger a refresh
