issues.summary: Customer Wallet Option Management (spec 027c)
issues.description:
Spec: .specify/specs/027c-wallet-options-management/spec.md

Overview

Implement customer-facing wallet management operations that let an authenticated user list, view, create, update, and remove saved wallet options. Customer is derived from the authenticated request context — never from caller-supplied email or customer number.

Dependencies

Spec 003 (PCI observability), spec 006 (customer authentication), spec 007 (customer identity integration), spec 010 (request feature-flag context), spec 016 (platform principal identity), spec 018 (PaymentMethodType alignment), spec 027a (WalletOption normalization).

Scope

- Expose GET /api/v1/payments/wallet-options, GET /api/v1/payments/wallet-options/{id}, POST /api/v1/payments/wallet-options, PUT /api/v1/payments/wallet-options/{id}, DELETE /api/v1/payments/wallet-options/{id} under the Payments MVC area.

- Return PCI-safe masked display metadata only; never return raw PAN, CVV, PIN, gift-card number, or encrypted secrets in responses, logs, traces, or idempotency replays.

- Discriminated create/update request models by paymentMethodType; no legacy polymorphic DTOs on the public surface.

- Credit-card PAN allowed on create only; update rejects PAN replacement.

- Default credit-card behavior through UpdateWalletOption with isDefault = true.

- Idempotency-Key required on all write operations; replay returns sanitized response without duplicate Wallet side effects.

- Delegate to legacy Wallet / Customer Service / payment-method-specific service boundaries; no direct legacy SQL writes.

Out of Scope

Checkout tender normalization (spec 027a), encrypted transient secret storage (spec 027b), payment authorization/capture/refund/void, invoice finalization, direct Wallet SQL.

Acceptance Criteria

- Authenticated customer can list/retrieve wallet options without raw payment data.

- Credit-card wallet option can be created and used as a saved WalletOptionReference during checkout normalization (027a).

- Updating card expiration/default state changes the Wallet option without allowing PAN replacement.

- Removing a Wallet option prevents future checkout use while preserving historical order references.

- Write-operation idempotency prevents duplicate legacy Wallet mutations; raw payment secrets never stored, compared, logged, or replayed.

- Unsupported mutation attempts fail deterministically with WALLET_OPTION_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED.

issues.summary: Payment Tokenization and Wallet Instrument Normalization (spec 027a)
issues.description:
Spec: .specify/specs/027a-payment-tokenization-wallet-instrument-normalization/spec.md

Overview

Implement the checkout/payment orchestration phase that converts caller-supplied payment tenders into normalized, PCI-safe execution references before route snapshot lookup or adapter execution.

Dependencies

Spec 003 PCI observability, spec 018 PaymentMethodType alignment, spec 023 payment plan validation, spec 024 tokenized adapter references, payment pipeline spec v2.11 sections 8.5 and 16.6.

Scope

- Accept RawInstrument or WalletOptionReference tender inputs on POST /orders; exactly one source shape per caller-supplied tender.

- Tokenize raw/transient credit-card and Apple Pay inputs through approved PaymentProcessing boundaries.

- Create, reuse, or resolve legacy Wallet-backed references, including parent card Wallet options, linked external token options, direct payment-method-key options, gift cards, account balance, Apple Pay, and known legacy tender shapes.

- Import finalized invoice TenderCouponApplications[] as invoice-sourced payment tenders and reject ad hoc coupon-code tender inputs on POST /orders.

- Persist only PCI-safe Wallet/reference lineage, masked display metadata, and executed processor context; never persist raw PAN, CVV, PIN, raw Apple Pay payloads, encrypted secret payloads, or transient secret handles.

- Revalidate balance-backed tenders after saga suspension before execution resumes.

Out of Scope

Adapter execution, card processor-specific behavior, SCA continuation after adapter invocation, encrypted transient verification-secret storage (spec 027b), customer-facing WalletOption management APIs (spec 027c), Wallet schema ownership, and direct legacy SQL writes.

Acceptance Criteria

- Raw card, saved card with CVV, raw gift card with PIN, saved gift/account-balance options, Apple Pay payloads, and invoice-sourced tender coupons normalize to the correct execution reference shape before adapters run.

- Saved WalletOption input validates customer/channel ownership, active/deleted/expired state, payment-type compatibility, and required verification-secret presence before normalization succeeds.

- Stored cards produce or reuse the legacy parent credit-card Wallet option and linked external Wallet option containing the PaymentMethodKey when Versant execution requires it.

- Known legacy Wallet payment types map according to the spec matrix and unsupported Phase 1 methods fail deterministically without fabricating PaymentMethodKey values.

- Tokenization retries are idempotent and reuse the original normalized reference for the same orchestration request id.

- Tests prove sensitive inputs are absent from durable saga, order, journal, idempotency, log, trace, exception, and support payloads.

issues.summary: Payment Adapter Contract and Non-Scarcity Reservation Semantics (specs 024-025)
issues.description:
Context

Specs 024-025 cover two related checkout execution foundation slices for the order-processing service:

- Spec 024 (.specify/specs/024-payment-adapter-contract-credit-card/spec.md) defines the payment adapter boundary, action-specific request/result contracts, adapter capability declarations, adapter resolution, the balance-query seam, and the CreditCard reference adapter wrapping the existing PaymentProcessing client.

- Spec 025 (.specify/specs/025-non-scarcity-inventory-reservations/spec.md) evolves inventory reservation semantics so non-scarcity domains such as GolfNowSubscription can pass checkout Block 3 without a provider-side hold while scarce domains such as TeeTime retain full hold lifecycle behavior.

These belong together because they prepare checkout execution for real side-effect boundaries: payment adapters must execute only through a normalized, PCI-safe capability contract, and reservation semantics must distinguish scarce holds from intentional non-scarcity no-op success before checkout orchestration composes inventory and payment blocks.

Scope

- Define a single IPaymentAdapter interface for AuthorizeAsync, CaptureAsync, CreditAsync, and VoidAsync.

- Define action-specific request/result types for AUTH, CAPTURE, CREDIT, and VOID.

- Add strongly typed adapter capability declarations containing the matrix dimensions needed by validation, decisioning, and execution.

- Add PaymentAdapterFactory resolution by canonical PaymentMethodType.

- Define IBalanceQueryAdapter as the seam for later balance-backed methods.

- Implement the CreditCard reference adapter around GolfNow.Payment.APIPaymentProcessingClient using tokenized payment references.

- Normalize provider declines and expected validation failures to non-throwing adapter outcomes.

- Keep adapter logging and observability compliant with PCI constraints from spec 003.

- Extend inventory reservation contracts with explicit non-scarcity success classification distinct from unsupported-domain behavior.

- Add domain reservation policy/configuration for scarce versus non-scarcity-enabled domains, including GolfNowSubscription support.

- Ensure checkout Block 3 treats non-scarcity reservation outcomes as success while preserving TeeTime hold lifecycle behavior.

- Support deterministic non-scarcity no-op outcomes for reserve, extend, confirm, and release.

- Add tests for adapter resolution, capability declarations, CreditCard auth/capture/credit/void normalization, PCI-safe request validation/logging, non-scarcity-only checkout semantics, mixed scarce/non-scarce invoices, compensation release behavior, confirm behavior, and unsupported-domain distinction.

Out of Scope

- Gift card, account balance, affiliate, ApplePay, and funded coupon adapter implementations.

- Payment execution orchestration, journals, decision engine/failover, SCA challenge flow, scheduled payments, or tokenization implementation beyond requiring tokenized input.

- Subscription pricing logic changes.

- Subscription entitlement consumption logic.

issues.summary: Entitlement Providers and Payment Plan Validation (specs 022-023)
issues.description:
Context

Specs 022-023 cover two related checkout foundation slices for the order-processing service:

- Spec 022 (.specify/specs/022-entitlement-provider-implementations/spec.md) implements Phase 1 provider surfaces for loyalty and benefit entitlements, including consume and reverse operations, idempotency, audit references, compensation behavior, and explicit exclusion of funded coupons because they are payment tenders.

- Spec 023 (.specify/specs/023-payment-domain-model-plan-validation/spec.md) defines the payment sub-aggregate embedded in saga_checkout and validates a checkout payment plan before route snapshot lookup or adapter execution.

These belong together because checkout needs a clean boundary between entitlements and tenders before payment adapters run. Loyalty and benefit consumption can affect checkout state and compensation, while payment plan validation ensures finalized invoices, tenders, charge allocations, merchant grouping, zero-dollar behavior, and unsupported payment methods are resolved before any payment side effects start.

Scope

- Define or implement IEntitlementProvider surfaces for Loyalty and Benefit entitlement types.

- Support entitlement consume and reverse operations with provider-level request idempotency.

- Persist enough entitlement consumption provider reference data to support later reversal and audit.

- Map expected entitlement provider outcomes to checkout/post-purchase taxonomy without throwing for business failures.

- Carry ActorContext from spec 016 on entitlement consumption and reversal records.

- Exclude FundedCoupon from entitlement handling and keep it in payment tender planning.

- Model payment state as a sub-aggregate inside saga_checkout, not as a separate payment saga collection.

- Build payment tenders, charge item allocations, computed distribution instructions, route snapshot grouping inputs, and payment attempt skeletons from a Finalized invoice.

- Validate tender amounts, tender currency, supported payment methods, missing component merchant ids, and zero-dollar/internal no-op classification before adapter execution.

- Group route snapshot inputs by (MerchantId, PaymentMethodType).

- Add focused tests for loyalty/benefit consume and reverse idempotency, compensation reversal, funded-coupon exclusion, payment plan construction, tender validation, merchant grouping, unsupported methods, and zero-dollar behavior.

Out of Scope

- Funded coupon entitlement handling; funded coupons are payment methods.

- Payment tender balance queries.

- Promo code validation/application during invoice pricing.

- Accounting policy for point breakage or benefit recognition.

- Full external loyalty partner webhook handling.

- Payment adapter interfaces or implementations.

- Payment execution, journals, circuit breaker/failover behavior, SCA challenge handling, or scheduled payments.

- Checkout saga orchestration beyond the entitlement provider surfaces and payment sub-aggregate shape.

Acceptance Criteria

- Spec 022 and 023 files reference this Jira ticket.

- Loyalty and Benefit entitlement provider surfaces support ConsumeAsync and ReverseAsync.

- Entitlement consume and reverse requests carry a request id and behave idempotently on retries.

- Consume results persist enough provider reference data to reverse later.

- Reverse treats already-reversed as a successful idempotent outcome.

- Checkout consumes only benefits flagged by pricing as requiring Block 4 consumption.

- FundedCoupon is not modeled as an entitlement and is handled only as PaymentMethodType.FundedCoupon in payment planning.

- Expected entitlement provider outcomes such as Insufficient, Unavailable, AlreadyConsumed, AlreadyReversed, and ValidationFailed map to non-throwing result statuses.

- Entitlement consumption and reversal records carry ActorContext from spec 016.

- Post-purchase entitlement reversal defers to spec 014 adjustment decision outputs; refund-only decisions do not reverse entitlements unless explicitly required.

- Payment state is modeled as a sub-aggregate inside saga_checkout, not as saga_sales_order_payment.

- Payment plan creation only operates on Finalized invoices.

- PaymentTender.PaymentMethodType uses the canonical enum from spec 018.

- Charge item allocations are created from due-online component amounts and associated sales tax only; due-at-facility values are excluded from online tender obligations.

- Distribution instructions include revenue target, amount, revenue category, optional merchant routing context, and refundable financial metadata without inferring operational cancellation ability.

- Payment plan validation rejects missing component MerchantId, tender currency mismatch, tender total mismatch, and unsupported payment methods before route snapshot lookup or adapter side effects.

- Route grouping is deterministic by (MerchantId, PaymentMethodType).

- Zero-dollar orders without payment-method-on-file requirements classify for InternalNoOp; zero-dollar orders with payment-method-on-file requirements require a validation/auth-capable tender.

- Business-rule rejection paths return ResultWrapper-compatible errors and do not throw for expected validation failures.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

References

- Specs: .specify/specs/022-entitlement-provider-implementations/spec.md, .specify/specs/023-payment-domain-model-plan-validation/spec.md

- Related: specs 001, 002, 012, 014, 016, 018, 020, payment pipeline spec v2.11

- Parent docs: docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-pipeline-spec.md, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-entities.md, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-payment-pipeline-spec-v2.md

- Epic: CORE-14269

issues.summary: Inventory Reservation Implementations (spec 021)
issues.description:
Context

Spec 021 covers the Phase 1 inventory reservation provider path for the order-processing service:

- Spec 021 (.specify/specs/021-inventory-reservation-implementations/spec.md) implements the shared inventory reservation contract for TeeTime inventory and establishes explicit deferred behavior for Subscription and Timelyst domains.

This belongs as its own implementation slice because checkout Block 3 and compensation need provider-level reserve, confirm, release, and extend behavior before checkout orchestration can safely depend on durable inventory holds. The work also prevents non-TeeTime domains from accidentally routing through TeeTime reservation code before their domain-specific implementations are ready.

Scope

- Implement IInventoryReservationProvider for TeeTime inventory.

- Add provider factory/registry resolution by item group domain.

- Support reserve, confirm, release, and extend operations for TeeTime holds.

- Use orchestration-generated provider request ids for provider-level idempotency.

- Map item-level ItemQuantity with Quantity.Type=Players to TeeTime provider player count.

- Return orchestration InventoryHoldId and provider DomainHoldId from reserve operations.

- Return fulfillment/booking evidence from confirm operations for downstream fulfillment workflows.

- Classify reservation failures as retryable infrastructure, unavailable inventory, validation, already-completed, or terminal provider failures.

- Add explicit Subscription and Timelyst placeholder/deferred provider behavior until those domain implementations land.

- Add tests for TeeTime reserve, confirm, release, extend, idempotent retries, invalid quantity handling, provider resolution, unsupported domains, and failure classification.

Out of Scope

- Checkout saga implementation itself.

- Payment authorization or capture.

- Full Subscription and Timelyst reservation provider implementations.

- Physical attendance or no-show policy.

- Repricing during reservation.

- Post-purchase cancellation decision logic; confirmed inventory release/cancel remains gated by spec 014 adjustment decisions.

Acceptance Criteria

- Spec 021 file references this Jira ticket.

- TeeTime implements IInventoryReservationProvider for reserve, confirm, release, and extend operations.

- Provider resolution is based on ItemGroup.Domain and cannot route Subscription or Timelyst item groups to TeeTime reservation logic.

- TeeTime reservation maps Item.Quantity.Value with Quantity.Type=Players to the provider player count.

- TeeTime reservation rejects non-whole, non-positive, or non-Players quantities with ResultWrapper-compatible validation/business errors.

- Reserve, confirm, release, and extend accept an orchestration-generated request id and behave idempotently on retries.

- Reserve returns both an orchestration InventoryHoldId and provider DomainHoldId.

- Confirm returns fulfillment or booking evidence required by spec 015.

- Release is idempotent and treats already-released as a successful outcome.

- Post-purchase release or provider-side cancellation of confirmed inventory requires an approved spec 014 cancellation decision for the item group; refundability alone is not sufficient.

- Extend uses provider-default hold extension where available and distinguishes retryable from terminal failures.

- Subscription and Timelyst provider behavior is explicit, deferred, and test-covered until their domain specs land.

- Expected provider outcomes map to checkout error taxonomy without throwing for unavailable inventory, validation, already-completed, or unsupported-domain cases.

- Reservation code preserves item-level ItemQuantity semantics and never reads currency from ItemGroup.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

References

- Spec: .specify/specs/021-inventory-reservation-implementations/spec.md

- Related: specs 002, 009, 012, 014, 015, 020

- Parent docs: docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-pipeline-spec.md, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-entities.md, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-payment-pipeline-spec-v2.md

issues.summary: Invoice Modification, Reprice, and Finalization (specs 019-020)
issues.description:
Context

Specs 019-020 cover the remaining mutable invoice workflow before checkout:

- Spec 019 (.specify/specs/019-invoice-modification-reprice/spec.md) defines invoice modification and explicit reprice behavior so clients can edit active invoices, refresh expired invoices intentionally, preserve ItemQuantity, and rerun pricing, discounts, allocation, and estimated tax.

- Spec 020 (.specify/specs/020-invoice-finalization/spec.md) defines invoice finalization so an Active invoice becomes the hard customer-facing quote required before checkout, including availability re-checks, stale pricing refresh, authoritative tax calculation or fallback tax, and refundability snapshot capture.

These belong together because finalization depends on the mutation/reprice semantics: expired invoices must be explicitly repriced before finalization, price-affecting edits invalidate finalized quotes, and both flows enforce version-key conflict handling, checkout-lock rejection, item-level currency, and ItemQuantity preservation.

Scope

- Add invoice modification endpoint: PUT /api/v1/invoicing/channels/{channelId:int}/invoices/{invoiceId}.

- Add explicit invoice reprice endpoint: POST /api/v1/invoicing/channels/{channelId:int}/invoices/{invoiceId}/reprice.

- Add invoice finalization endpoint: POST /api/v1/invoicing/channels/{channelId:int}/invoices/{invoiceId}/finalize.

- Support adding/removing item groups and items, changing ItemQuantity, and adding/removing promo codes before checkout.

- Re-run pricing, benefit discounts, promo discounts, revenue allocation, and estimated tax for modifications and reprices.

- Reprice expired invoices explicitly without changing GET behavior.

- Enforce version-key conflict handling and checkout-lock rejection across modification, reprice, and finalization.

- Transition price-affecting changes to Finalized invoices back to Active.

- Finalize Active invoices by re-checking availability, refreshing stale item pricing, replacing estimated tax with final or fallback tax, and persisting refundability snapshots.

- Preserve corrected invoice model constraints: ItemQuantity travels as a value object, CurrencyCode is item-level only, and ItemGroup carries no currency.

- Add focused tests for update, reprice, finalization, stale version keys, invalid statuses, checkout locks, currency mismatches, removed item warnings, tax fallback, and refundability snapshot enforcement.

Out of Scope

- Checkout order creation, purchase locking beyond rejecting locked invoices, payment authorization/capture, reservations, entitlement consumption, or post-purchase item cancellation.

- Tax provider implementation details beyond consuming spec 011 contracts.

- Inventory reservation holds.

- Post-purchase adjustment decisions.

- Changing GET behavior to auto-reprice expired invoices.

Acceptance Criteria

- Spec 019 and 020 files reference this Jira ticket.

- PUT invoice modification requires the current versionKey and returns INVOICE_VERSION_CONFLICT for stale updates without modifying the invoice.

- PUT and reprice reject Purchased and checkout-locked invoices with domain-specific ResultWrapper-compatible errors.

- Invoice mutation accepts and persists item quantity only as ItemQuantity (Value + Type) and never as scalar/unit sibling fields.

- ItemGroup does not accept, persist, or return CurrencyCode; top-level invoice currency is derived from uniform item-level currencies.

- Modified and repriced invoices rerun pricing, tier selection, benefit discounts, promo discounts, revenue allocation, and estimated tax.

- Cross-currency modified, repriced, or finalized invoices fail with INVOICE_CURRENCY_MISMATCH.

- Explicit reprice can transition an Expired invoice back to Active when at least one item remains available.

- GET on an expired invoice remains read-only and does not auto-reprice.

- Partial item removal during modification or reprice returns a Warning response with removed item details.

- Price-affecting changes to a Finalized invoice transition it back to Active and require re-finalization.

- Finalize requires the current versionKey, operates only on Active invoices, rejects Expired invoices with reprice guidance, and rejects checkout-locked invoices.

- Finalize re-checks availability for every item and re-queries pricing only for stale PricingValidUntilUtc items unless availability changes require removal.

- Finalize performs a hard tax provider calculation when available and may persist EstimatedFallback tax only when spec 011 fallback conditions are satisfied.

- Finalize persists a non-null RefundabilitySnapshot on every purchasable component.

- Successful modification, reprice, and finalization all generate a new VersionKey.

- Mutating endpoints are protected by the global idempotency-key contract.

- Business-rule rejection paths return ResultWrapper-compatible errors and do not throw for expected validation failures.

issues.descriptionHtml:
Context

Specs 019-020 cover the remaining mutable invoice workflow before checkout:

  • Spec 019 (.specify/specs/019-invoice-modification-reprice/spec.md) defines invoice modification and explicit reprice behavior so clients can edit active invoices, refresh expired invoices intentionally, preserve ItemQuantity, and rerun pricing, discounts, allocation, and estimated tax.

  • Spec 020 (.specify/specs/020-invoice-finalization/spec.md) defines invoice finalization so an Active invoice becomes the hard customer-facing quote required before checkout, including availability re-checks, stale pricing refresh, authoritative tax calculation or fallback tax, and refundability snapshot capture.

These belong together because finalization depends on the mutation/reprice semantics: expired invoices must be explicitly repriced before finalization, price-affecting edits invalidate finalized quotes, and both flows enforce version-key conflict handling, checkout-lock rejection, item-level currency, and ItemQuantity preservation.

Scope

  • Add invoice modification endpoint: PUT /api/v1/invoicing/channels/{channelId:int}/invoices/{invoiceId}.

  • Add explicit invoice reprice endpoint: POST /api/v1/invoicing/channels/{channelId:int}/invoices/{invoiceId}/reprice.

  • Add invoice finalization endpoint: POST /api/v1/invoicing/channels/{channelId:int}/invoices/{invoiceId}/finalize.

  • Support adding/removing item groups and items, changing ItemQuantity, and adding/removing promo codes before checkout.

  • Re-run pricing, benefit discounts, promo discounts, revenue allocation, and estimated tax for modifications and reprices.

  • Reprice expired invoices explicitly without changing GET behavior.

  • Enforce version-key conflict handling and checkout-lock rejection across modification, reprice, and finalization.

  • Transition price-affecting changes to Finalized invoices back to Active.

  • Finalize Active invoices by re-checking availability, refreshing stale item pricing, replacing estimated tax with final or fallback tax, and persisting refundability snapshots.

  • Preserve corrected invoice model constraints: ItemQuantity travels as a value object, CurrencyCode is item-level only, and ItemGroup carries no currency.

  • Add focused tests for update, reprice, finalization, stale version keys, invalid statuses, checkout locks, currency mismatches, removed item warnings, tax fallback, and refundability snapshot enforcement.

Out of Scope

  • Checkout order creation, purchase locking beyond rejecting locked invoices, payment authorization/capture, reservations, entitlement consumption, or post-purchase item cancellation.

  • Tax provider implementation details beyond consuming spec 011 contracts.

  • Inventory reservation holds.

  • Post-purchase adjustment decisions.

  • Changing GET behavior to auto-reprice expired invoices.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Spec 019 and 020 files reference this Jira ticket.

  2. PUT invoice modification requires the current versionKey and returns INVOICE_VERSION_CONFLICT for stale updates without modifying the invoice.

  3. PUT and reprice reject Purchased and checkout-locked invoices with domain-specific ResultWrapper-compatible errors.

  4. Invoice mutation accepts and persists item quantity only as ItemQuantity (Value + Type) and never as scalar/unit sibling fields.

  5. ItemGroup does not accept, persist, or return CurrencyCode; top-level invoice currency is derived from uniform item-level currencies.

  6. Modified and repriced invoices rerun pricing, tier selection, benefit discounts, promo discounts, revenue allocation, and estimated tax.

  7. Cross-currency modified, repriced, or finalized invoices fail with INVOICE_CURRENCY_MISMATCH.

  8. Explicit reprice can transition an Expired invoice back to Active when at least one item remains available.

  9. GET on an expired invoice remains read-only and does not auto-reprice.

  10. Partial item removal during modification or reprice returns a Warning response with removed item details.

  11. Price-affecting changes to a Finalized invoice transition it back to Active and require re-finalization.

  12. Finalize requires the current versionKey, operates only on Active invoices, rejects Expired invoices with reprice guidance, and rejects checkout-locked invoices.

  13. Finalize re-checks availability for every item and re-queries pricing only for stale PricingValidUntilUtc items unless availability changes require removal.

  14. Finalize performs a hard tax provider calculation when available and may persist EstimatedFallback tax only when spec 011 fallback conditions are satisfied.

  15. Finalize persists a non-null RefundabilitySnapshot on every purchasable component.

  16. Successful modification, reprice, and finalization all generate a new VersionKey.

  17. Mutating endpoints are protected by the global idempotency-key contract.

  18. Business-rule rejection paths return ResultWrapper-compatible errors and do not throw for expected validation failures.

issues.summary: Platform Principal, Accounting Facts, and Payment Method Alignment (specs 016-018)
issues.description:
Context

Specs 016-018 cover three related foundation slices for the order-processing service:

- Spec 016 (.specify/specs/016-platform-principal-identity/spec.md) defines a consistent platform principal and actor context model so transactional records can be audited back to the authenticated API credential or well-known system actor that initiated work.

- Spec 017 (.specify/specs/017-accounting-facts-export/spec.md) defines lean accounting fact fields and events so Finance/Accounting systems can consume deterministic business facts without embedding ASC 606 policy in order-processing.

- Spec 018 (.specify/specs/018-payment-method-type-alignment/spec.md) aligns the canonical PaymentMethodType values before payment adapters and checkout tenders build on them.

These belong together because they are cross-cutting contract/model groundwork: identity stamping feeds audit and accounting events, accounting exports depend on fulfillment/current-item facts and principal audit context, and payment method alignment keeps tender/cash-movement facts stable before later payment adapter work.

Scope

- Define PlatformPrincipal, ActorContext, principal resolution contracts, scoped request principal access, and well-known system principals.

- Add principal/actor stamping requirements to invoices, orders, credit memos, saga starts, payment attempts, adjustment overrides, fulfillment events, and accounting fact events where applicable.

- Define flat permission strings needed by adjustment override paths and future admin actions.

- Add minimal accounting fact fields for item timing, item quantity propagation, fulfillment evidence snapshots, and component product classification.

- Define purchase, fulfillment, credit memo, and no-show accounting fact event shapes that contain facts only.

- Enforce prohibited accounting-policy fields so order-processing does not persist ASC 606 conclusions.

- Align canonical Phase 1 PaymentMethodType values: CreditCard, GolfNowGiftCard, EzlGiftCard, AccountBalance, Affiliate, ApplePay, and FundedCoupon.

- Add legacy payment-method normalization for known historical values without accepting deprecated aliases on public wire contracts.

- Add focused tests for principal resolution/stamping, permission checks, accounting fact event shaping/prohibited fields, payment-method canonical serialization, unsupported method validation, and funded-coupon placement.

Out of Scope

- Authentication mechanism implementation, user provisioning, IAM administration, or RBAC UI.

- Customer identity replacement; customer identity remains separate from platform principal identity.

- ASC 606 policy engine, performance-obligation conclusions, seller-of-record legal conclusions, GL mapping, ERP posting, or close-process workflow.

- Payment adapter implementation or payment execution.

- Full accounting warehouse/reporting design.

- Public endpoint exposing principal details.

Acceptance Criteria

- Spec 016, 017, and 018 files reference this Jira ticket.

- PlatformPrincipal and ActorContext models are defined without coupling Core to ASP.NET HttpContext.

- Request-scoped and system principal access patterns support HTTP handlers, sagas, hosted services, and event-driven workflows.

- Permission checks use flat string set membership and support spec 014 adjustment override permissions.

- Transactional records stamped by this feature preserve immutable creator principal context and mutable last-modified principal context where applicable.

- Accounting fact models/events include item quantity, service timing, fulfillment evidence, component merchant/product classification, payment/cash movement references, and principal audit metadata where applicable.

- Accounting fact models/events contain business facts only and do not persist prohibited ASC 606 policy conclusion fields.

- Canonical Phase 1 PaymentMethodType values bind, serialize, and validate with stable PascalCase wire names.

- FundedCoupon is treated as a payment tender and not an entitlement type.

- Deprecated GiftCard, unsupported future methods, and unknown payment methods fail validation before adapter resolution.

- Legacy payment-method normalization supports known historical spellings for migration/internal use without exposing public aliases.

- Business-rule rejection paths return ResultWrapper-compatible errors and do not throw for expected validation failures.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

References

- Specs: .specify/specs/016-platform-principal-identity/spec.md, .specify/specs/017-accounting-facts-export/spec.md, .specify/specs/018-payment-method-type-alignment/spec.md

issues.summary: Fulfillment Model (spec 015)
issues.description:
Context

Spec 015 (.specify/specs/015-fulfillment-model/spec.md) introduces durable item-level fulfillment tracking for the order read model. The goal is to make current item state explicit for post-purchase adjustment decisions, no-show decisions, support workflows, accounting evidence, and downstream consumers.

For Phase 1, fulfillment is a purchase/entitlement concept, not physical attendance. A tee time is fulfilled when the booking is confirmed on the third-party tee sheet and confirmation is received. Physical golfer attendance remains separate and is handled by no-show workflows.

Scope

- Add fulfillment event modeling to the order document.

- Add current item-group fulfillment state projection on the order read model.

- Preserve ItemQuantity semantics for fulfilled, pending, cancelled, and unfulfilled quantities.

- Track fulfillment source, external reference, occurrence time, recording time, and compact fulfillment evidence.

- Support Pending, Fulfilled, PartiallyFulfilled, Unfulfilled, and Cancelled item-level fulfillment states.

- Maintain top-level order fulfillment status derived from item-group state.

- Add Phase 1 immediate-capture behavior and future-compatible capture-strategy fields without enabling deferred capture.

- Feed fulfillment state into spec 014 post-purchase adjustment provider context.

- Ensure fulfilled items can be non-cancellable while still potentially refundable depending on provider policy.

- Add focused unit coverage for fulfillment event application, quantity validation, current-state projection, idempotency, and post-purchase context integration.

Out of Scope

- Domain-specific fulfillment trigger implementation for TeeTime, Subscription, Timelyst, or add-on providers.

- Deferred capture / delayed payment execution, fulfillment-triggered partial capture, authorization-window extension, and accounts-receivable recovery.

- Physical delivery or shipping tracking.

- Revenue recognition accounting rules.

- Facility-side fulfillment system integration beyond contracts/events needed by this service.

- Public fulfillment administration UI.

Acceptance Criteria

- Order model supports fulfillmentEvents[] with stable event identity, event type, item-group references, ItemQuantity fulfilled amounts, source metadata, external reference, occurrence time, recorded time, and Phase 1 capture fields.

- Order model supports current item-group fulfillment state projection with purchased, fulfilled, pending, cancelled, and unfulfilled quantities.

- Order top-level fulfillment status derives from all item-group fulfillment states.

- Fulfillment events are idempotent by stable eventId and/or domain externalReference where available.

- Event application preserves ItemQuantity.Type and rejects unit conversion/mismatched quantity types.

- Phase 1 defaults every item to immediate capture and fulfillment events do not trigger payment actions.

- Deferred capture values are treated as future-state only and cannot bypass checkout Block 5 capture.

- Unfulfilled events feed post-purchase adjustment evaluation rather than directly issuing refunds or voids in Phase 1.

- Spec 014 adjustment policy context receives per-item fulfillment state including status, fulfilled quantity, pending quantity, and relevant fulfillment timestamps/evidence.

- No-show logic can distinguish tee-time booking fulfillment from physical attendance/no-show outcomes.

- Credit memo and adjustment execution remain responsible for financial refund state; fulfillment events update operational/current purchase state only.

- Business-rule rejection paths return ResultWrapper-compatible errors and do not throw for expected validation failures.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

issues.summary: Post-Purchase Adjustment Decision Engine (spec 014)
issues.description:
Context

Spec 014 (.specify/specs/014-refund-decision-engine/spec.md) introduces a centralized post-purchase adjustment decision engine. The engine consults domain-specific policy providers and produces per-item-group cancellation/refundability decisions plus a complete net-effect manifest / credit memo blueprint when financial movement is available.

This broadens the original refund-only framing: cancellation ability and refundability are separate decisions. For example, a completed tee time may no longer be operationally cancellable, but it may still be refundable through weather, goodwill, support, or other policy paths.

Scope

- Define IPostPurchaseAdjustmentDecisionEngine and the core orchestration flow.

- Define IAdjustmentPolicyProvider and provider factory contracts for per-domain policy evaluation.

- Define adjustment request, line-item adjustment, cancellation decision, refundability decision, override, policy response, net-position, tender allocation, support-action, and decision-result models.

- Load order, purchase invoice, checkout payment state, and prior credit memos before evaluation.

- Compute net refundable position from applied credit memos and purchase-time refundability snapshots.

- Validate requested quantity type, remaining refundable amount, cancellation ability, refundability, and override permissions.

- Merge provider decisions into per-item-group adjustment decisions and a credit memo blueprint including fees, warnings, overrides, tender allocation, support/manual actions, and orderRefundVersionAtCreation.

- Add focused unit coverage for cancellation/refundability separation, engine orchestration, rejection paths, fees, tender caps, fallback handling, override audit behavior, and idempotency.

Out of Scope

- Credit memo persistence and lifecycle implementation itself (spec 013).

- Fulfillment model implementation (spec 015), beyond accepting nullable fulfillment state as input to policy providers.

- Payment CREDIT execution, tax adjustment execution, inventory release execution, and operational cancellation execution.

- Customer-facing refund/cancellation request API endpoint design.

- Admin override UI.

- Concrete TeeTime, Subscription, or Timelyst policy rules beyond interface contracts and test doubles/stubs needed by this feature.

Acceptance Criteria

- IPostPurchaseAdjustmentDecisionEngine.EvaluateAsync accepts a PostPurchaseAdjustmentRequest and returns a PostPurchaseAdjustmentDecisionResult.

- IAdjustmentPolicyProvider interface is defined; IAdjustmentPolicyProviderFactory resolves by domain.

- Engine loads order, purchase invoice, checkout saga/payment state, and prior credit memos before evaluating.

- Engine calls the correct domain provider for each affected item group.

- For every affected item group, the result includes an explicit cancellation decision and refundability decision.

- Cancellation request types reject or route manual resolution when any requested item group is not automatically cancellable, without suppressing available refundability details.

- Refund-only request types may approve financial refunds for item groups that are not operationally cancellable.

- Request quantities validate ItemQuantity.Type against the purchased item, and provider contexts/credit memo blueprints preserve ItemQuantity.

- Provider responses are correctly merged into the adjustment decision and net-effect manifest.

- netRefundAmount equals gross refund credits minus total fees.

- Tender resolution distributes the net refund across tenders respecting per-tender caps and provider preferences.

- Admin overrides are permission-gated, applied, and audited.

- Original-tender-unavailable scenarios resolve through channel fallback policy or reject with REFUND_NO_VALID_TENDER when no fallback exists.

- Engine is idempotent for identical requests using the same request id on output.

- Business-rule rejection paths return ResultWrapper-compatible errors and do not throw.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

issues.summary: Credit Memo Entity (spec 013)
issues.description:
Context

Spec 013 (.specify/specs/013-credit-memo-entity/spec.md) introduces a first-class CreditMemo entity for post-purchase adjustments (refunds, fees, discretionary credits) as a typed sibling to Purchase invoices.

This fills the structural gap for item-level refund auditability and gives refund orchestration a durable financial-adjustment document.

Scope

- Add InvoiceType discriminator support (Purchase, CreditMemo) in the invoices collection model.

- Define and persist the CreditMemo shape (status lifecycle, reason metadata, signed line items, totals, allocation resolution, side-effect state).

issues.summary: Invoice Property Relocation (spec 012)
issues.description:
Context

Spec 012 (.specify/specs/012-invoice-property-relocation/spec.md) realigns the Order Processing invoice model after requirements review found several properties on the wrong entity level.

The implementation starts from branch docs/invoice_enhancements and should follow the existing Spec-Kit workflow before code changes.

Scope

- Move PricingTier and PricingTierSavings from item components up to invoice items.

- Move MerchantId from invoice items down to item components.

- Replace loose item quantity fields with a required ItemQuantity value object (Value + QuantityType).

- Introduce PaymentLocationAmount for DueOnline and DueAtFacility at component, item, and invoice totals levels.

- Add purchase-time RefundabilitySnapshot metadata on item components and expose the customer-facing refundability projection.

- Update domain models, wire contracts, converters, pricing provider contracts/stubs, invoice builder merchant derivation, totals calculation, and tests.

Out of Scope

- Retrofitting spec 005; spec 012 owns this post-F3 alignment.

- Payment pipeline implementation beyond wire/spec alignment.

- Saga implementation for checkout.

- DueOnlineLater or additional payment-location categories.

- MongoDB migration unless persisted pre-GA invoices exist in the target environment.

Acceptance Criteria

- Item has item-level PricingTier, PricingTierSavings, and required ItemQuantity; it no longer has item-level MerchantId.

- ItemComponent has component-level MerchantId, PaymentLocationAmount-typed DueOnline/DueAtFacility, and RefundabilitySnapshot.

- InvoiceResponse exposes the corrected item/component placement, PaymentLocationAmountResponse, refundability response, and invoice Totals.

- InvoiceBuilder.DeriveMerchantIds() derives the top-level merchant list from all item components with case-insensitive de-duplication.

- Pricing provider contracts and the in-memory pricing provider return item-level tier/quantity values and component-level merchant/refundability values.

- Totals follow spec 012: TotalDue = DueOnline.Amount + DueOnline.SalesTax; TotalTax = DueOnline.SalesTax + DueAtFacility.SalesTax.

- Unit/integration tests are updated for the new shape and all existing tests pass.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

References

- Epic: CORE-14269

- Example ticket shape: CORE-14439

- Spec: .specify/specs/012-invoice-property-relocation/spec.md

- Parent docs branch: docs/invoice_enhancements

issues.summary: Tax control plane on gn-svc-platform — TaxProvider + TaxProviderProfile (spec authoring)
issues.description:
Context

CORE-14443 introduces a production ITaxProvider abstraction in gn-api-orderprocessing (Vertex Phase 1, Avalara + SensibleWeather to follow). Every provider call needs a stored configuration — endpoint, credentials, currencies, remit responsibility — and that configuration must live on gn-svc-platform, paralleling the existing payment-processor control plane.

This ticket covers the platform-side work: new TaxProvider and TaxProviderProfile entities with full CRUD + CSFLE-encrypted credentials + admin HTTP surface + seed task. Without this landed, CORE-14443 has nowhere to load Vertex credentials from at call time, so this ticket is a hard upstream of CORE-14443's Phase 1.

Spec authored at docs/tax-control-plane-spec.md on the feature branch. Scope is spec authoring only at this stage — /plan, /tasks, and implementation are follow-up tickets after spec review.

Scope

- TaxProvider entity (collection taxProviders) — analog of PaymentProcessor. Carries ProviderKey slug + typed FieldSchema[] declaring profile field shape (name / type / isSecret / isRequired / description).

- TaxProviderProfile entity (collection taxProviderProfiles) — analog of MerchantPaymentProfile. References TaxProvider by id + MerchantAccount by id (the existing Merchant of Record in this repo). Carries ConfigFields (plaintext) + ConfigSecrets (CSFLE-encrypted, reusing ICsfleFieldEncryptor).

- Save-time schema validation — required/declared/type checks + "no secrets in plaintext blob" guard. Factored into reusable FieldSchemaValidator.

- HTTP surface under /api/v1/TaxProcessing/ mirroring the PaymentProcessing area — full CRUD on both entities, includeSecrets query parameter on profile GET.

- Tasks console tax-seed command to upsert the Vertex provider + gn-vertex-default profile tied to GolfNow's primary MerchantAccount.

- HTTP Basic auth over TLS for order-processing → platform (no new credential).

- Observability via existing ActivitySource, with secret keys/values never logged.

Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] docs/tax-control-plane-spec.md authored covering every capability above with the data-model tables, HTTP surface, validation rules, and CSFLE reuse points.

- [ ] Scope boundary explicit — reader can tell that /plan, /tasks, implementation, admin portal UI, per-provider test-call endpoint, multi-region replication, and cache-invalidation push are out of this ticket.

- [ ] References to the existing payment-processor files used as the structural template (PaymentProcessor.cs, MerchantPaymentProfile.cs, MerchantPaymentProfileValidator.cs, MerchantPaymentProfileRepo.cs, CsfleServiceCollectionExtensions.cs).

- [ ] Reference to docs/csfle-overview.md for the broader encryption posture.

- [ ] User-directed naming changes honored: TaxProfile → TaxProviderProfile, AccountOwner → typed MerchantId FK to MerchantAccount.

- [ ] Open items from the inbound order-processing contract either resolved in spec or carried forward as [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] for the platform team.

- [ ] No /plan, no /tasks, no code, no DI changes, no new csprojs in this ticket.

Out of Scope

- /plan and /tasks breakdown (follow-up ticket).

- Implementation of any C# files (follow-up ticket).

- Admin portal UI work.

- Per-provider credential test-call endpoint.

- Multi-region replication of TaxProvider/TaxProviderProfile.

- Cache-invalidation push from platform to order-processing.

- Renaming sweep on the order-processing pipeline spec (TaxAccountConfiguration → TaxProviderProfile) — order-processing's concern.

Relationship to CORE-14443

This ticket is a hard upstream of CORE-14443 (Finish-to-Start Dependency — CORE-14443 FS-depends on this one). Order-processing's Vertex adapter cannot read credentials at call time without the platform endpoint this spec defines. Linked as FS-Depends-On.

References

- Inbound draft contract from order-processing (pasted into planning conversation, 2026-05-04).

- Plan file: ~/.claude/plans/i-am-working-on-unified-popcorn.md.

- gn-api-orderprocessing pipeline spec §9.3 / §9.4 (authoritative platform vs orchestration split).

- gn-svc-platform existing payment-processor area — structural template.

---
Built with Claude assistance (Opus 4.7 1M)

Spec authored and formalized

Three commits on branch feature/CORE-14445-0 (worktree at C:\Users\206565609\source\repos\GolfNowEng\_worktrees\gn-svc-platform\feature-CORE-14445-0). Not yet opened as a PR — reviewing before push.

Commits:

- c6fbd01 — Initial implementation spec at docs/tax-control-plane-spec.md

- 99b752c — §12 Audit trail and change history (trigger extension, shared audit log, existing controllers serve new entity types)

- 17db32a — Spec-Kit artifacts at .specify/specs/002-tax-control-plane/

Shape: 6 user stories (P1 ×3, P2 ×2, P3 ×1), 30 functional requirements, 14 success criteria, 14 edge cases.

- P1 — admin manages TaxProvider; admin manages TaxProviderProfile (with CSFLE secrets + MerchantAccount FK); order-processing reads profile with cascading-inactive signal.

- P2 — save-time field-schema validation (presence / declaredness / type / misplaced-secret); audit log + entity history for tax entities via existing trigger and controllers.

- P3 — tax-seed console command, idempotent.

Resolved during planning (from inbound contract draft):

- Merchant of Record reference → existing MerchantAccount entity (FK pattern copied from MerchantPaymentProfileValidator lines 17–23).

- Identity shape → ObjectId + ProviderKey slug on TaxProvider; ObjectId on TaxProviderProfile. Matches repo convention, diverges from inbound draft's slug-PK suggestion.

- Schema validation → full typed FieldSchema with reusable FieldSchemaValidator helper. Richer than PaymentProcessor.RequiredParams.

- Phase 1 scope → full CRUD on both entities + tax-seed task. Not read-only.

- Entity names → TaxProvider / TaxProviderProfile (renamed from inbound's ProviderInterface / TaxProfile); AccountOwner free-text replaced with typed MerchantId FK.

- Audit/history → extend existing changeStreamHistoryAudit.js trigger + reuse existing AuditLogController / EntityHistoryController (currently under /api/v1/PaymentProcessing/ — vestigial naming; cross-cutting rename deferred to a future standalone ticket, captured in plan's Complexity Tracking).

Carried forward as [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] for /tasks:

- Exact Vertex field list for the tax-seed command — pending confirmation with the order-processing team during contract review for CORE-14443. Working set (companyCode, endpoint, trustedKey, apiUser) is stubbed and mutable via admin CRUD after seeding, so the implementation is not blocked.

Constitution check: PASS on all 7 principles (v4.4.0). Section IV marked N/A — MongoDB-only feature. Optimistic Concurrency subsection (v4.2.0) specifically addressed: Guid.CreateVersion7(), BsonBinaryData filter pattern, MatchedCount == 0 → 409.

Authority chain: inbound draft contract from gn-api-orderprocessing team (2026-05-04, pasted into planning conversation); docs/csfle-overview.md; existing PaymentProcessing area files as the copy template; constitution Sections I, II, III, V, VI, VII.

Relationship to CORE-14443: CORE-14445 FS-depends on CORE-14443 via Finish-to-Start Dependency link. Order-processing's Vertex adapter cannot load credentials at call time until this platform-side work lands.

Next step: /speckit tasks to generate the executable task breakdown from plan.md. This ticket closes when the spec + plan are approved and merged.

Note: Built with Claude assistance (Opus 4.7 1M)

issues.summary: F6/F7 — Tax provider abstraction + response archival (spec authoring)
issues.description:
Context

Replaces the current StubEstimatingTaxProvider with a production-shaped tax abstraction. Unblocks F5 (Invoice Finalization), F9–F10 (Checkout Block 6 CommitTax), and F18–F20 (post-purchase tax adjustments). See plan at ~/.claude/plans/what-s-next-to-work-reactive-panda.md.

Scope is one focused ticket, spec authoring only at this stage. /plan and /tasks come in a follow-up ticket after spec review.

Scope — F6 Tax Provider Abstraction

- Substrate-neutral ITaxProvider covering the four tax phases from pipeline §9: estimate, finalize, commit, reversal (void / credit).

- Tax rate store with soft-TTL read semantics; Mongo-backed Phase 1 behind a substrate-neutral abstraction (DynamoDB swap deferred).

- Vertex Phase-1 adapter as the only concrete provider.

- EstimatedFallback behaviour on provider outage when rate store has a (stale) entry. Cold-store + unreachable = hard failure.

Scope — F7 Tax Provider Response Archival

- Per-operation archival of raw provider request/response pairs to durable object storage, out-of-band from the hot path.

- Retention + lifecycle aligned with 7y business retention.

- PCI/PII redaction before archival.

Acceptance Criteria

issues.summary: Add Rate Set Fee Support to New Transaction Fee Retrieval Stored Procedure
issues.description:
As part of the Customizable Transaction Fees initiative, the first ticket introduced a parallel transaction fee retrieval path by creating a new stored procedure that retrieves fees outside of the Tee Time Search stored procedure.

The current implementation supports retrieving transaction fees by:

- FacilityID

- OwnerID (existing behavior)

However, the roadmap requires rate set–level fee overrides, which are currently impossible with the legacy stored procedure.

This ticket introduces the ability for the new transaction fee stored procedure to retrieve fees by GolfCourseID, enabling the first step toward full fee customization.

The legacy stored procedure remains unchanged.

---
Goal

Extend the new transaction fee stored procedure to support retrieving fees by GolfCourseID, allowing the system to apply the proper fee hierarchy:

- Rate Set level (highest priority)

- Facility level

- Owner level (default baseline)

The API will continue using the toggle introduced in Ticket #1.

---
Scope

Enhance the new transaction fee stored procedure so that it can:

- Accept GolfCourseID as an optional parameter

- Retrieve fees defined at the Rate Set level

- Fallback to facility/owner fees when rate set fees are not defined

The legacy stored procedure remains unchanged.

Additionally, objects that surface transaction fee data to the client must be updated to support the new hierarchy.

This specifically includes:

- FeeMessagingDisplayRates

The FeeMessagingDisplayRates object must be updated to ensure that rate set–level fees retrieved via GolfCourseID are properly represented in the fee messaging and display layer, including correct fee amounts and hierarchy source when applicable.

---
Functional Requirements

Stored Procedure Enhancements

Update the new transaction fee stored procedure to support:

New Parameter

Parameter

Type

Description

GolfCourseID

Nullable

Enables lookup of Rate Set–level transaction fees

---
Fee Resolution Logic

Fees should resolve using the following hierarchy:

1. Rate Set Fee

If a fee exists for:

GolfCourseID + OwnerID

Use the Rate Set fee.

---
2. Facility Fee

If no rate set fee exists:

GolfFacilityID + OwnerID

Use the Facility fee.

---
3. Owner Fee

If neither of the above exist:

OwnerID

Use the Owner default fee.

---
Returned Data

The stored procedure should return all fee data required by the API including:

- Fee Type

- Fee Amount

- Refundable flag

- Taxable flag (if currently available)

- Fee source level

- RateSet

- Facility

- Owner

---
API Changes

When the toggle parameter is enabled, the following endpoints must pass GolfCourseID into the new fee stored procedure when available.

Affected endpoints:

- API 2.1 GetTeeTimes

- API 2.1 GetInvoice

- API 2.1 TeeTimeInvoice

- Reservation Service — Invoice call

- API 2.1 GetFacilitySummaries  - for FeeMessagingDisplayRates

When the toggle is disabled, the system continues using the legacy stored procedure.

---
Acceptance Criteria

Functional

Stored procedure accepts GolfCourseID

Fee hierarchy works correctly:

GolfCourseID → FacilityID → OwnerID

If a Rate Set fee exists, it overrides facility/owner fees.

If no rate set fee exists, the system falls back correctly.

---
API Behavior

When toggle is enabled:

- API passes GolfCourseID to the new stored procedure

- Fee is resolved using hierarchy logic

- Invoice totals are composed in the application layer

- FeeMessagingDisplayRates reflects the correct fee source and amount

When toggle is disabled:

- Legacy stored procedure is used

- API responses remain unchanged

---
Backward Compatibility

- Legacy stored procedure remains unchanged

- Existing production behavior remains identical when the toggle is off

issues.summary: LaunchDarkly Request Context Builder (spec 010)
issues.description:
Context

Every LaunchDarkly flag evaluation in gn-api-orderprocessing today goes through a single static context — Context.New("service:order-processing") hardcoded in LaunchDarklyInvoiceTtlResolver. No channel targeting, no customer targeting, no regional targeting. A "5% rollout" against that one service key is all-or-nothing in practice.

CORE-14438 (in-flight) introduces ILaunchDarklyContextFactory with a single-kind service context that adds a region custom attribute. Spec 010 extends that factory — it does not replace it — by adding a request-scoped multi-context with three kinds (channel, customer, service) so flag rules can target (channel, customer, region, saga-role) tuples.

Three context kinds

- channel — key = channelId from the route (32-bit signed integer, base-10 string-encoded). Attributes extensible; none required initially.

- customer — key = customerId (UUIDv7, canonical lowercase string). Attributes: country, isGuest, authenticationMethod. Omitted when ICustomerIdentityAccessor.Current == null.

- service — key = service:order-processing (preserves CORE-14438 compatibility). Attributes: region (from CORE-14438) + new isSagaActiveRegion derived from the lease store.

Locked design decisions

- Saga-region source — consume ILeadershipLeaseStore + RegionalSagaOptions.CurrentRegion directly from CORE-14438. Blocked by CORE-14438 merging to develop.

- ChannelId source — route only. Migrate InvoicesController endpoints from /api/v1/invoicing/invoices to /api/v1/invoicing/channels/{channelId:int}/invoices. Remove ChannelId from CreateInvoiceRequest wire body; re-attach as typed int on CreateInvoiceCommand.

- ChannelId type correction — the canonical ChannelId in GolfNow's domain is a 32-bit integer. CreateInvoiceRequest.ChannelId and InvoiceResponse.ChannelId on develop are currently typed Guid; spec 010 corrects both to int.

- Country seam — extend CORE-14421's CustomerIdentity record with string Country = "US". HttpContextCustomerIdentityAccessor hardcodes US until Profile Service emits a country claim. No separate resolver abstraction.

- Anonymous behavior — omit the customer kind from the multi-context when ICustomerIdentityAccessor.Current == null. Channel + service always present.

Scope

In scope:

- Extend ILaunchDarklyContextFactory with CreateRequestContext() returning a multi-context.

- New IRequestLdContextScope (scoped) caching the built Context per request.

- Three per-kind builders (ChannelContextKindBuilder, CustomerContextKindBuilder, ServiceContextKindBuilder).

- isSagaActiveRegion attribute on the service kind, derived from CurrentRegion == LeadershipLease.HolderRegion with fail-closed semantics on lease-read failure.

- Migration of LaunchDarklyInvoiceTtlResolver to consume IRequestLdContextScope (proof the seam works end-to-end).

- Route refactor for InvoicesController (POST + GET) — /channels/{channelId:int}/... prefix. [FromRoute] int channelId on both actions.

- Retype CreateInvoiceRequest.ChannelId (removed from wire body) and InvoiceResponse.ChannelId (stays on response body) from Guid to int.

- CustomerIdentity record extension with string Country = "US" + WebApi accessor hardcode.

- Unit + integration test coverage (Integration trait for end-to-end route + captured-context assertions).

Out of scope:

- Profile Service integration for real customer country (seam present, follow-up ticket).

- Channel attributes beyond channelId.

- New feature flags (infrastructure only; existing flags adopt the context automatically).

- Mediator pipeline-level ambient-context injection.

- Saga-originated flag evaluation (no HttpContext; handled by future alternate scope).

Dependencies

- Blocked by CORE-14438 (spec 008 regional saga control plane). ILaunchDarklyContextFactory, RegionalSagaOptions, and ILeadershipLeaseStore must exist on develop before implementation starts. This ticket currently delivers groundwork only — spec.md + this ticket + worktree; no code changes until the block clears.

- Speckit flow (/speckit skill) will generate plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, quickstart.md, contracts/*, and tasks.md in a follow-up pass.

Constitution alignment

- Principle VIII — ILeadershipLeaseStore and LD abstractions stay in Core; driver code stays in Repository.Mongo.

- Principle IX — lease-read failure logs a Warning and returns isSagaActiveRegion = false (fail closed); does not throw.

- Principle XII — wire contract isolation: ChannelId removed from CreateInvoiceRequest wire body; moves to a typed int ChannelId parameter on CreateInvoiceCommand.

Spec location

.specify/specs/010-launchdarkly-request-context-builder/spec.md on branch features/CORE-14439-01 (branched from develop, committed at 61de486, pushed to origin). Worktree: ~/source/worktrees/gn-api-orderprocessing/features-CORE-14439-01. See the spec file for the full Data Types dictionary (ChannelId, CustomerId, InvoiceId, VersionKey, Country, AwsRegion, IsSagaActiveRegion, and all LD kind keys + attributes).

Acceptance criteria

- AC1 — Authenticated request with channelId (integer) on the route produces a multi-context containing all three kinds with expected attrs.

- AC2 — Anonymous request with channelId on the route produces a multi-context with channel + service only (customer omitted).

- AC3 — isSagaActiveRegion flips based on RegionalSagaOptions.CurrentRegion == LeadershipLease.HolderRegion.

- AC4 — A lease-read failure returns isSagaActiveRegion = false, logs a Warning, and the request still completes.

- AC5 — LaunchDarklyInvoiceTtlResolver evaluates invoice-ttl and invoice-pricing-ttl against the new multi-context with existing fallback behavior preserved.

- AC6 — Kiota-generated OrderProcessingApiClient reflects the new /channels/{channelId:int}/invoices route shape on build; the regenerated ChannelId on both CreateInvoiceRequest (removed) and InvoiceResponse (int) builds green for consumers.

issues.summary: Regional Saga Control Plane — spec 008 readiness review + impl
issues.description:
Scope

Pre-implementation readiness review of Speckit feature 008 (Regional Saga Control Plane), plus the implementation PRs that follow once the review clears. Phase 0 in this ticket is read-only against docs/* — harmonization gaps get classified and filed, not fixed in this PR.

Phase 0 deliverables (this PR)

#

Work

Deliverable

1

Relocate untracked files onto ticket branch

.specify/specs/008-regional-saga-control-plane/, .specify/specs/009-saga-execution-safety/, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing_regional-saga-spec.md

2

Mechanical heading renumber inside 008 package

# 003 — → # 008 — in spec.md, plan.md, research.md, tasks.md

3

Spec-package integrity audit

No placeholders; 7 ACs trace to tasks; phases 1a–1e fully covered; constitution refs live

4

Cross-spec consistency check

F1/F2 dependencies landed; F#### internal refs reconciled against folder numbers; duplicate 006- prefix logged

5

Harmonization memo vs docs/*

Per-doc section citing regional content, flagging conflicts/gaps, classifying MUST/SHOULD/NICE

Background

Spec 008 delivers the multi-region coordination machinery for leader-scoped saga execution (MongoDB-backed global leadership lease, regional monitor, SNS→SQS router, endpoint lifecycle, LaunchDarkly override, observability) plus single-region mode used by dev/stg. issues.summary: Migrate idempotency + customer-auth caches from Redis to Valkey
issues.description:
Context

gn-api-orderprocessing currently uses AWS ElastiCache for Redis 7.x as the substrate for two concerns:

- Idempotency response cache (FR-016 / entities spec §14) — landed under CORE-14041 (F1).

- Customer-auth token validation cache (CORE-14419) — landed this sprint in GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.Authentication.Customer/Caching/RedisCustomerTokenCache.cs.

After Redis Inc. relicensed under SSPL/RSAL in March 2024, AWS launched ElastiCache for Valkey (the Linux-Foundation OSS fork) in October 2024. Valkey is wire-compatible with Redis (RESP protocol preserved), so StackExchange.Redis continues to work unchanged — but the platform, naming, and configuration references across our code and docs need to be migrated so we're operating on the OSS track going forward.

This story is the application-side switch. The infrastructure provisioning (ElastiCache Valkey cluster) is tracked in CORE-14405 (rescoped from Redis → Valkey).

Scope

In-scope

- Client wiring & configuration

- src/GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.Repository.Redis/ — rename project to Repository.Valkey (folder, .csproj, namespaces, DI extension methods AddOrderProcessingRedis* → AddOrderProcessingValkey*).

- RedisConnectionFactory, RedisKeyBuilder, RedisCustomerTokenCache (CORE-14419) → rename to Valkey* equivalents; keep StackExchange.Redis as the client library (still the AWS-recommended Valkey client).

- Config key rename: ConnectionStrings:Redis → ConnectionStrings:Valkey; RedisOptions → ValkeyOptions.

- appsettings*.json / Octopus variable placeholders: #{Redis.ConnectionString} → #{Valkey.ConnectionString}.

- Documentation

- CLAUDE.md project section — replace Redis references (Persistence Conventions, Dependencies, ElastiCache sidebar).

- docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-pipeline-spec.md + docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-entities.md §14 — rewrite the Redis chapter to Valkey.

- .specify/memory/constitution.md Principle VIII and related sections.

- Auto-memory entries (feedback_idempotency_is_redis.md, repository-split entry) refreshed after ticket lands.

- Tests

- tests/GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.Repository.Redis.Tests/ → rename + update.

- Testcontainers-managed integration tests: swap the redis:7 image for valkey/valkey:8 (or equivalent AWS-aligned tag).

- CI / deploy

- Octopus variable set rename; no new environment provisioning (that's CORE-14405).

Out-of-scope

- Provisioning the Valkey cluster itself — CORE-14405.

- Changing the cache semantics (TTL, key pattern, fail-closed behavior, SET NX EX atomic first-write) — only the engine identity changes.

- Replacing StackExchange.Redis with a different client library — remains the canonical choice for Valkey per AWS guidance.

Acceptance criteria

- All production .cs, .csproj, .slnx, .json, and .yml files reference Valkey, not Redis, for the idempotency + customer-auth caches.

- Repository.Redis project renamed to Repository.Valkey with folders, namespaces, and DI registrations updated.

- CLAUDE.md, docs/*.md, .specify/memory/constitution.md updated; no stale Redis references outside historical commit messages and archived speckit documents.

- Existing idempotency + customer-auth integration tests pass against a Valkey container image.

- Connection-string config key renamed end-to-end (appsettings, Octopus, Secrets Manager references).

- All PR checks green; LogTemplateAllowlistTests unaffected (no new log template tokens introduced).

Dependencies

- Blocked by: CORE-14405 (ElastiCache Valkey provisioning — rescoped from Redis).

- Related: CORE-14041 (F1 persistence foundations), CORE-14419 (customer-auth cache introduced the second Redis touchpoint).

Notes

- StackExchange.Redis ≥ 2.8.x is the AWS-documented client for ElastiCache for Valkey — no library swap required.

- Valkey preserves the RESP2/RESP3 protocol, SET NX EX, EXPIRE, and AUTH semantics we rely on, so no behavioral changes are expected.

- Naming rename is load-bearing for future reviewers: "Repository.Redis" holding a Valkey client would be a trap.

issues.summary: Customer-auth integration wave: F3 endpoint wiring + speckit backfill + mediator identity context
issues.description:
Scope

Consolidation wave following CORE-14419 (customer-auth infrastructure). Four deliverables under one branch, stacked sequentially. No new user-facing feature.

Four-step plan

#

Work

Deliverable

1

Backfill speckit spec for CORE-14419 as-shipped

.specify/specs/006-customer-authentication/ (spec, plan, tasks, research, quickstart, contracts/)

2

Harden customer-auth Redis cache with Polly resilience (circuit breaker + tight timeout)

RedisCustomerTokenCache wrapped in named ResiliencePipeline; new contracts/redis-resilience.md; 5 new configurable options

3

Design + ship standard mechanism for customer-identity propagation into mediator commands/queries

.specify/specs/007-customer-identity-integration/ + Core abstraction seam + Core pipeline behavior + WebApi adapter

4

Decorate F3 invoice endpoints with [CustomerAuthentication(Required)] + ownership check on GET

InvoicesController changes + handler refactor to consume identity context

Background

CORE-14419 shipped dual-auth infrastructure (X-GolfId-Token / X-Customer-Token validator, handler, middlewares, Redis cache, DI wiring) in 5 commits on features/CORE-14419-01. The ticket description punted two follow-ups: "Rolling out the attribute to existing controllers — follow-up tickets after infrastructure merges."

Four gaps remain to close before F4 Invoice Modification:

- Documentation. CORE-14419 bypassed the speckit workflow — no 006-* folder exists. The as-shipped contract (dual-header mutual exclusion, Profile Service validator shape, cache TTL semantics, claim types, error codes) lives only in code + tests.

- Cache resilience. RedisCustomerTokenCache calls IConnectionMultiplexer directly with the 5s multiplexer default timeout and no circuit breaker. Auth path is latency-sensitive; a hung Redis hammers every customer-scoped request. Fail-open handling exists but isn't fail-fast.

- Integration. The [CustomerAuthentication] attribute is NOT decorating any endpoint. InvoicesController carries only [Authorize] (PlatformPrincipal).

- Identity propagation. CreateInvoiceCommand reads customerId from the request body — anyone can claim any identity. No ICurrentCustomer / ICustomerIdentityAccessor exists anywhere in Core. IdempotencyMiddleware reads the claim directly off HttpContext.User, which is too coupled to the web layer for handlers to reuse.

Design — Redis cache resilience (Step 2)

Polly v8 ResiliencePipeline named "CustomerAuth.Cache" wraps every RedisCustomerTokenCache operation.

- Timeout strategy — per-call budget, default 150ms (configurable via Auth:CustomerAuthentication:CacheOperationTimeoutMs).

- Circuit breaker strategy — default 20% failure ratio over a 30s rolling window, min 10 calls, 10s break duration, 1 probe in half-open. All configurable: CacheBreakerFailureRatio, CacheBreakerSamplingWindowSeconds, CacheBreakerMinimumThroughput, CacheBreakerBreakDurationSeconds.

- No retry — cache is an optimization; a failed cache read falls straight through to the validator (which has its own retry policy via AddStandardResilienceHandler). Retries here would extend latency with no correctness benefit.

- Fail-open preserved — pipeline exceptions (TimeoutRejectedException, BrokenCircuitException) surface to the existing catch-all in TryGetAsync/SetAsync, which treats them as cache miss. No call-site changes elsewhere.

- Observability — new counters customer_auth.cache.timeouts and customer_auth.cache.breaker_state{state=open|half-open|closed} on CustomerAuthDiagnostics.

Design — Mediator customer-identity propagation (Step 3)

Explicit over ambient. Follows GNC's LoginCommand(LoginRequest, string IpAddress) pattern — additional request-context metadata is a command constructor parameter, not hidden scope state. Testability wins over implicit ambient access.

- New CustomerIdentity record (Core): (Guid CustomerId, string? CustomerNumber, string? Email, bool IsGuest, CustomerTokenType Source).

- New ICustomerIdentityAccessor (Core) with Current (nullable) and GetRequired() (throws — contract violation per Principle IX when authz should have blocked).

- HttpContextCustomerIdentityAccessor (WebApi) reads CustomerClaimTypes.CustomerId/… from HttpContext.User; derives Source from the authenticationMethod claim.

- ICustomerScopedRequest marker interface on commands/queries that require customer context.

- CustomerIdentityBehavior<TRequest,TResponse> pipeline behavior (after ValidationBehavior, before LoggingBehavior) returns ResultWrapper.Forbidden with messageType=CUSTOMER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED for scoped requests with no identity — belt-and-suspenders against future non-HTTP dispatchers.

- Commands gain CustomerIdentity Customer as an explicit ctor param; controller populates from the accessor before mediator.Send(...).

Design — F3 endpoint wiring (Step 4)

- POST /api/v1/invoicing/invoices → [CustomerAuthentication(Mode = Required)]. Authenticated claim overrides any customerId in the wire DTO (which is removed from CreateInvoiceRequest entirely).

- GET /api/v1/invoicing/invoices/{id} → [CustomerAuthentication(Mode = Required)] with ownership check. Handler compares stored invoice.customerId == claim.CustomerId; mismatch → 403 with new INVOICE_ACCESS_DENIED = 10403 error code.

- CreateInvoiceRequest.CustomerId removed (breaking change to Kiota client — safe because no consumer callers exist yet).

Branch + worktree

- Cut from: features/CORE-14419-01 HEAD (bf834b5), not develop.

- Worktree: $WORKTREE_BASE/gn-api-orderprocessing/features-CORE-14421-01.

- Rebase onto develop after CORE-14419 PR merges.

- Work folder: $JIRA_DOCS/CORE-14421/.

Sequence

One PR with four stacked commits:

- docs(speckit): backfill 006-customer-authentication spec for CORE-14419 (CORE-14421)

- feat(security): Polly circuit breaker + tight timeout on customer-auth Redis cache (CORE-14421)

- feat(security): ICustomerIdentityAccessor + CustomerIdentityBehavior for mediator customer-scoped handlers (CORE-14421)

- feat(invoicing): [CustomerAuthentication(Required)] on F3 endpoints + ownership check on GET (CORE-14421)

Acceptance

- Step 1: .specify/specs/006-customer-authentication/ exists with spec.md, plan.md, research.md, tasks.md, quickstart.md, and contracts/ (dual-header-mutual-exclusion, profile-service-validator, customer-claim-types, redis-cache-key-format, error-codes-customer-auth).

- Step 2: RedisCustomerTokenCache wraps Redis calls in the named CustomerAuth.Cache pipeline; timeout fires at 150ms; circuit breaker trips after 20% failures over 30s; customer_auth.cache.timeouts counter increments under a slow Redis; fail-open passthrough still returns null from TryGetAsync (validator still called). New contracts/redis-resilience.md documents the contract.

- Step 3: ICustomerIdentityAccessor + HttpContextCustomerIdentityAccessor + ICustomerScopedRequest + CustomerIdentityBehavior landed; unit tests cover missing-identity (Forbidden) and spoofed-identity (body-trumped-by-claim) paths; behavior-registration-order test asserts CustomerIdentityBehavior runs after ValidationBehavior, before LoggingBehavior.

- Step 4: POST /api/v1/invoicing/invoices without a customer token → 401 CUSTOMER_TOKEN_REQUIRED. GET /api/v1/invoicing/invoices/{id} with a mismatched customer claim → 403 INVOICE_ACCESS_DENIED. CreateInvoiceCommand no longer reads customerId from request body — authoritative value comes from the claim. IdempotencyMiddleware continues to scope keys per customer (no regression).

- Kiota regenerates with CreateInvoiceRequest no longer carrying CustomerId.

- Full-settings test profile passes (Testcontainers Mongo + Redis + Authentication.Customer integration scenarios).

Dependencies

- Depends on: CORE-14419 (infrastructure — branch-stacked; rebases onto develop after CORE-14419 merges).

- Related: CORE-14418 (F3 endpoints being decorated), CORE-14411 (F23 PCI observability — log property allowlist may need CustomerIdentity-derived fields).

- Unblocks: F4 Invoice Modification (PUT/reprice) — identity propagation must be idiomatic before that ships.

Out of scope

- Rolling the attribute onto non-invoice endpoints (none yet warrant it).

- Publishing Authentication.Customer as a NuGet package (separate ticket).

- F4 Invoice Modification.

- Replacing the PlatformPrincipal scheme.
