issues.summary: Create Automated Job to Remove LIT Holds When Salesforce SO Block Is Received
issues.description:
Background

Currently, when a golf course submits a Salesforce Sales Order Block (SO Block) for trade times, the associated Locked In Trade (LIT) holds remain on the tee sheet.

There is:

- No automated process to remove the related LIT holds

- No queue or notification for manual cleanup

- No system correlation between CRM.SalesforceBlockTrade and tee sheet holds

This creates operational risk, oversell potential, and manual intervention requirements.

---
Problem

When a Sales Order Block is created in Salesforce:

- The related LIT tee sheet holds are not removed

- The tee sheet continues to reflect capacity as blocked

- Operations must manually identify and remove holds

- There is no visibility or alert that reconciliation is required

---
Proposed Solution

Create a background job/task that:

- Listens for or reads records from CRM.SalesforceBlockTrade

- Identifies the associated LIT tee sheet holds

- Automatically removes/cancels the corresponding holds from the tee sheet

- Logs activity for history of updates. Ensure updates are made to the Reservation.ReservationHold table

---
Functional Requirements

- System must query or receive updates from CRM.SalesforceBlockTrade

- Job must:

- Match SO Block to correct course, date range

- Identify related LIT holds on the tee sheet

- Remove or cancel those holds automatically

- System should log:

- SO Block ID

- Course (Play Facility ID)

- Dates affected

- of holds removed

- Timestamp

---
Acceptance Criteria

- Given an SO Block is created in Salesforce
When the job processes the record
Then the corresponding LIT tee sheet holds are removed automatically

- No manual intervention is required to reconcile holds

- System logs clearly show:

- SO Block processed

- Holds removed successfully

- No impact occurs to:

- Non-LIT holds

- Standard trade inventory

---
Dependencies

- Access to CRM.SalesforceBlockTrade

- Link Results to Reservation.ReservationHold

- Confirmed mapping logic between:

- Salesforce SO Block

- Course ID

- Date/time range

- LIT hold identifiers

  1. Listens for or reads records from CRM.SalesforceBlockTrade

  2. Identifies the associated LIT tee sheet holds

  3. Automatically removes/cancels the corresponding holds from the tee sheet

  4. Logs activity for history of updates. Ensure updates are made to the Reservation.ReservationHold table

Functional Requirements

  • System must query or receive updates from CRM.SalesforceBlockTrade

  • Job must:

    • Match SO Block to correct course, date range

    • Identify related LIT holds on the tee sheet

    • Remove or cancel those holds automatically

  • System should log:

    • SO Block ID

    • Course (Play Facility ID)

    • Dates affected

    • of holds removed

    • Timestamp

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given an SO Block is created in Salesforce
    When the job processes the record
    Then the corresponding LIT tee sheet holds are removed automatically

  • No manual intervention is required to reconcile holds

  • System logs clearly show:

    • SO Block processed

    • Holds removed successfully

  • No impact occurs to:

    • Non-LIT holds

    • Standard trade inventory

Dependencies

  • Access to CRM.SalesforceBlockTrade

  • Link Results to Reservation.ReservationHold

  • Confirmed mapping logic between:

    • Salesforce SO Block

    • Course ID

    • Date/time range

    • LIT hold identifiers

issues.summary: Loyalty - Points Not Subtracting for Cancelled Reservations
issues.description:
Golfers booking a TT online, receive GP Points but the cancellation via IVR or Website does not subtract the points earned for this reservation.

This issue is related to a previous ticket - TTSUPPORT-7119: GolfPass Rewards Points not being subtracted after cancelling Planning

Example:
bsteiner23@gmail.com
This account is placing approx. 10 Reservations a day and cancelling while within the courses policy.
The below Canceled Reservations have all retained the points earned upon booking:
418274535- Canceled the same day, 13 hours after booking (256 pts)
418380252- Canceled the same day, 9 hours after booking (251 pts)
418351863- Canceled the same day, 9 hours after booking (241 pts)

Replication:

- Reservation placed by non-GP member, using a credit card as the method of payment.

- Points are placed on the ‘Pending’ list, set to apply to the account on the day of the TT

- TT is canceled before cancellation policy. This can be done via IVR or Website.

- Points remain to be applied after TT date has occurred.

- Actual: Code remains in ‘claimed’ status and cannot be applied to another tee time

issues.summary: Research and fix SQL Prompt issue in SSMS 22.4.1
issues.description:
Summary

There is an issue with SQL Prompt in SSMS 22.4.1. This problem arose after upgrading to the latest version.

Context

The issue occurred following an upgrade to SSMS version 22.4.1.

Error activating IHttpClientFactory
No matching bindings are available, and the type is not self-bindable.
Activation path:
7) Injection of dependency IHttpClientFactory into parameter httpClientFactory of constructor of type QtpApiFetcher
6) Injection of dependency IQtpApiFetcher into parameter qtpApiFetcher of constructor of type IndexAnalyzer
5) Injection of dependency IIndexAnalyzer into parameter indexAnalyzer of constructor of type IndexAnalysisResultViewModelFactory
4) Injection of dependency IIndexAnalysisResultViewModelFactory into parameter indexAnalysisResultViewModelFactory of constructor of type QtpIndexesController
3) Injection of dependency IQtpIndexesController into parameter qtpIndexesController of constructor of type IndexAnalysisCommandController
2) Injection of dependency IIndexAnalysisCommandController into parameter indexAnalysisCommandController of constructor of type ShowIndexAnalysisAiCommand
1) Request for ShowIndexAnalysisAiCommand

Suggestions:
1) Ensure that you have defined a binding for IHttpClientFactory.
2) If the binding was defined in a module, ensure that the module has been loaded into the kernel.
3) Ensure you have not accidentally created more than one kernel.
4) If you are using constructor arguments, ensure that the parameter name matches the constructors parameter name.
5) If you are using automatic module loading, ensure the search path and filters are correct.

Acceptance criteria

- Research the SQL Prompt issue.

- Implement a fix for the identified problem.

Solution

Redgate released a new version where the issue was fixed. [https://productsupport.red-gate.com/hc/en-us/community/posts/34727409486493-SQL-Prompt-not-working-on-newest-SSMS-22-4-1-version]
After installed the new version released, SSMS v22.4.1 worked successfully.

issues.summary: Offering Type Mapping
issues.description:
Our production integration partners will use various different names for their Service categories and we will need a way to map those to standardized Service Categories on our platform.

Examples from Club Champion:

- Full Bag

- Full Bag (No Putter)

- Driver

- Iron

- Wedge

- Putter

On our system, we should have platform standard categories so we can make standardized API filters that do not require unique naming conventions. Please use the exact spelling provided below as this will likely be exposed to the UI and would like it to match.

Go Live Service Categories:

- Full bag fitting

- Driver fitting

- Iron fitting

- Wedge fitting

- Putter fitting

Requirements:

- Create standardized service categories

- These should be mapped by ID and not Name just in case the names change in the future

- Create a mapping table where we can map an integrators service names to our standardized names

- Example: We would map ClubChampion’s Full Bag to Full bag fitting

- Example: We would map GOLFTEC’s full_bag_fitting to Full bag fitting

- So when the Inventory API calls to get locations that contain a service for ServiceCategory=Full bag fitting, it would return both Club Champion and GOLFTEC’s locations that contain their version of full bag fittings

- Same for the time slots at an individual location, filtering for ServiceCategory=Full bag fitting should account for any category mapped to Full bag fitting

- We need the ability to add new standard service categories with a database update

- Example: if we wanted to start exposing Hybrid fittings, we could add a new category and start mapping new integrators to it

issues.summary: Timelyst - Replicate Cache Manager behavior
issues.description:
Overview

Replicate the legacy CacheManager QueueUtility behavior in the Timelyst Hangfire project. The CacheManager syncs tee time inventory from external booking systems (EZL, B9, AGI, USC, CC, etc.) into GolfNow's cache using a four-tier priority schedule system that determines sync frequency based on date range proximity.

Replace the legacy long-running console app (polling loop) with Hangfire-based scheduled jobs in gn-svc-timelyst.Hangfire.

Background — Legacy Schedule System

The legacy system uses three CRM SQL Server tables:

- CRMUniqueRackSchedule — Routing table that maps facility/interface/course to a schedule group via 4-tier waterfall: UniqueGolfCourseID > PlayFacilityID > InterfaceType > Global default

- CRMScheduleGroup — Named container grouping scheduling rules (e.g., "365 Day Schedule")

- CRMScheduleGroupDetail — Actual interval rules: "for days X through Y, sync every Z minutes" with Action type (Active/Reactive/SyncOnly)

SyncTypes (Action column):

- 0 = ActiveCacheAndSync — always fetch tee times

- 1 = ReactiveCacheAndSync — only fetch if tee times already exist in range

- 2 = SyncOnly — synchronize existing cached data only

Example 365-day schedule tiers:

Days Out

Frequency

Action

0–1

60 min (1 hr)

Active

2–7

120 min (2 hr)

Active

8–14

240 min (4 hr)

Active

15–30

480 min (8 hr)

Active

31–63

719 min (~12 hr)

Reactive

64–365

1439 min (~24 hr)

Reactive

Architecture — Hangfire Replacement

Infrastructure

Component

Technology

Job scheduler

Hangfire (Redis-backed)

Message queue

AWS SQS

Interface config

MongoDB (InterfaceConfiguration collection)

Schedule data

SQL Server (existing CRM tables, new Dapper repos)

Three-Layer Job Hierarchy

1. InterfaceConfigurationBootstrapJob (recurring, every 6 hours)

- Registered at startup — the only hardcoded job

- Reads MongoDB InterfaceConfiguration collection

- For each enabled interface: AddOrUpdate a ReconciliationJob

- Removes orphaned reconciliation jobs for disabled/deleted interfaces

2. CacheManagerScheduleReconciliationJob (per interface type, cron from MongoDB config)

- Queries all active facilities for this interface type from CRM SQL

- Resolves schedule per facility using 4-tier waterfall (UniqueGolfCourseID > PlayFacilityID > InterfaceType > Global)

- Creates/updates one Hangfire recurring job per facility + date-range tier

- Removes orphaned sync jobs for deactivated facilities

3. CacheManagerSyncJob (per facility + date range — SQS producer)

- Triggered by Hangfire cron (derived from Frequency in CRMScheduleGroupDetail)

- Publishes message to AWS SQS with: PlayFacilityID, InterfaceType, DaysOutStart, DaysOutEnd, Action

- A separate queue worker project processes sync items from SQS

Key Design Decisions

4-Tier Waterfall Resolution (Expanded from Legacy 3-Tier)

The legacy C# QueueUtility uses a 3-tier waterfall. The Hangfire version implements the full 4-tier waterfall from the [GolfCourse].[GetScheduleDetail] stored proc:

- UniqueGolfCourseID — most specific (course-level override)

- PlayFacilityID — facility-level override

- InterfaceType — interface default (e.g. "EZL"), where PlayFacilityID and UniqueGolfCourseID are NULL

- Global default — all nulls (least specific fallback)

One Job Per Facility Per Tier (Scale by Design)

Creates a Hangfire recurring job for every facility + date-range combination. E.g., 500 EZL facilities x 6 tiers = 3,000 recurring jobs. Scales horizontally by adding more Hangfire workers.

No 7-Day Window Chunking

The legacy system subdivides each range into 7-day windows. The Hangfire version uses detail ranges as-is from CRMScheduleGroupDetail — the 7-day windowing was a legacy implementation detail, not a business requirement.

Frequency-to-Cron Mapping

Legacy DB frequency values (59, 113, 239, etc.) were set just under round numbers to stagger polling. With cron-based scheduling, these are rounded up to clean cron intervals:

DB Frequency

Rounded To

Cron

59 min

60 min

0 */1 * * *

113 min

120 min

0 */2 * * *

239 min

240 min

0 */4 * * *

719 min

720 min

0 */12 * * *

1439 min

1440 min

0 0 */1 * *

ReactiveCacheAndSync Handled by Queue Worker

The Hangfire scheduler does NOT check for tee time existence. All Action types are enqueued to SQS on schedule. The queue worker handles Action=0 (always fetch), Action=1 (check existence first), and Action=2 (sync only).

Interface Configuration via MongoDB

Interface types are NOT hardcoded. A MongoDB InterfaceConfiguration collection drives which reconciliation jobs are registered. Supports enable/disable without redeployment, adding new interfaces by inserting a document, and per-interface reconciliation cron schedules.

What Replaces IsQueueable?

In the legacy system, IsQueueable checks elapsed time against the frequency. With Hangfire, the cron expression itself enforces the interval. The CRMUniqueRackQueueStatus table is replaced by Hangfire's built-in job execution history.

Data Access — New Repositories (Dapper)

Build new repositories in gn-svc-timelyst.Hangfire using Dapper against existing CRM SQL Server tables. Do NOT depend on legacy GolfNow.Data assemblies.

Required repository interfaces:

- IFacilityRepository — GetActiveFacilitiesByInterfaceAsync(interfaceType) — queries CRMGolfCourse joined with CRMUniqueGolfCourseMap

- IScheduleRepository — GetAllUniqueRackSchedulesAsync() and GetAllScheduleGroupDetailsAsync() — reads CRMUniqueRackSchedule and CRMScheduleGroupDetail

- IInterfaceConfigurationRepository — GetAllInterfacesAsync() — reads MongoDB InterfaceConfiguration collection

Implementation Tasks

- Create MongoDB InterfaceConfiguration collection schema and seed data

- Implement Dapper repositories (IFacilityRepository, IScheduleRepository) against CRM SQL tables

- Implement InterfaceConfigurationBootstrapJob (reads MongoDB, manages reconciliation job registrations)

- Implement CacheManagerScheduleReconciliationJob (per interface — resolves schedules, creates sync jobs)

- Implement 4-tier waterfall schedule resolution logic

- Implement FrequencyToCron mapping with clean interval rounding

- Implement CacheManagerSyncJob (SQS producer — publishes sync messages)

- Implement orphaned job cleanup for both reconciliation and sync jobs

- Configure SQS queue name via appsettings (environment-specific)

- Add DisableConcurrentExecution and AutomaticRetry(0) to all jobs

Migration Path

- Phase 1: Deploy alongside legacy QueueUtility (both running, legacy is primary). Queue worker is idempotent — duplicate messages are harmless.

- Phase 2: Validate Hangfire jobs produce correct SQS messages by comparing with legacy output.

- Phase 3: Disable legacy QueueUtility, Hangfire becomes primary.

- Phase 4: Remove legacy QueueUtility code and CRMUniqueRackQueueStatus dependency.

Reference

Full technical deep-dive with code examples, SQL schemas, and pseudocode: .claude/CacheManager-Schedule-System.md in the gn-svc-timelyst repository.

The Associated order is a blank order.

Compared to the correct orderID

The Associated OrderID is not correct.

Expected Results:

The Associated OrderID is the correct OrderID that contains the featured product.

Acceptance Criteria:

Resolve the issue that is causing mobile pay and check in orders with featured products to not associate the correct order for the featured product.

issues.summary: Update Fee Messaging Logic to Include Dynamic Transaction Fees
issues.description:
In order to display the correct fee messaging on the front end, we need to update our logic to account for dynamic transaction fees enabled in the Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees table.

Example:

- Revenue team updates trade transaction fees at FID 55 from $3.49 to $1.99

- This update is stored in Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees (not CRMOwnerGolfFacility)

- Current outcome: The API returns $3.49 fee messaging and therefore the UI displays this incorrect value

- Expected outcome: The API should return the $1.99 fee messaging in order for front end to display the correct value

Note: The transaction fee is correct at the invoice level, it’s just the Fee Messaging that needs updated

issues.summary: Match Play in Scorecards
issues.description:
Product/Feature Name: Match Play in scorecard

Product Manager: Allen Shoup

Other Stakeholders: Chris Lipsit

---
Executive Summary

Provide a 2-3 sentence overview of what this feature/product is and why it matters

What we're building: Building support for the match play game type / format in the Compete scorecard

Why we're building it: Match play is the most popular game in golf

Success looks like: Users can compete in Match Play rounds and are very clear on the scoring, standings and results as they progress through the round

---
Problem Statement & Context

The Problem

We don’t have support for match play format in Compete

Background Context

- Current state: They must use another app or a paper scorecard to tally results

- Pain points: Same as above

- Opportunity size: Considerable--opportunity to onboard new users or conquest users from other apps

Strategic Context

- Business objectives: Game type we’ve wanted to offer for a long time

- Product strategy alignment: 2025 roadmap

- Competitive landscape: Many other golf apps support this game type; 18Birdies, GHIN, TheGrint, etc.

---
Functional Requirements

Example scorecard and leaderboard UI built from comparisons to Excel example, paper scorecards and competitive apps: https://www.figma.com/design/puCwqv6xPdoWymA1KPXBp2/Match-Play-updates-2025?node-id=9-17&t=v2Iis0uUlwTiDMpc-4

Core User Stories

As a Compete user, I want to compete in match play and be clear on mid-match standings and post-round results across key interfaces.

- Story 1: As a golfer using the Compete group scorecard, I want to input match play hole results so that I can track head-to-head competition between players/teams

- Acceptance criteria:

- User can enter hole-by-hole results for match play format

- System clearly displays winner, loser, or tie for each hole

- Supports both individual and team match play formats

- Priority: High

- Story 2: As a golfer viewing the scorecard, I want to see competing scores for each hole so that I understand how the match outcome was determined

- Acceptance criteria:

- Display shows gross scores for gross rounds (no handicapping)

- Display shows net scores for net rounds (handicapping active)

- Supports individual player scores

- Supports team total scores

- Supports best ball team scoring (individual's best score for their team)

- Priority: High

- Story 3: As a golfer during a match, I want to see current match standings within the scorecard so that I know who's winning and by how much

- Acceptance criteria:

- Clearly shows which player/team is currently winning

- Displays tied matches appropriately

- Shows number of holes played that count toward scoring

- Shows current standing/position for each player/team

- Identifies what information requires the separate Leaderboards view (UXD-751)

- Priority: High

User Flows & Scenarios

Primary User Flow: Match Play Scorecard Entry

- User selects match play format and participants

- User enters scores for each hole as play progresses

- System calculates hole winners based on scoring format (gross/net/team)

- System updates match standings after each hole

- User can view current match status and standings

Alternative Flows:

- Team match play with multiple scoring formats

- Handicapped vs non-handicapped rounds

- Tie scenarios and tie-breaking rules

Entry Points: Compete group scorecard interface Exit Points: Leaderboards view for detailed standings, round completion summary

---
Design Requirements & Constraints

UX Principles & Guidelines

- Design principles: GN Compete group scoring principles

- Brand guidelines: GN Compete games/wagers brand

- Design system: GN Compete

Content Requirements

- See https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/UXD-755 for asset needs

Visual & Interaction Design

- Animation/motion: same as existing games/wagers UX

---
Open Questions for Design Team

See https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/CFE-1809

---
Resources & References

Research & Data

- [Links to user research reports]

- [Analytics dashboards or data]

- [Market research or competitive analysis]

Technical Documentation

Link any key documentation that would empower UX/Design team (such as API responses/JSON)

---
Appendix

Please list and link tickets associated with this effort

---
This PRD serves as the foundation for design work. Questions, concerns, or clarifications should be directed to the Product Manager before design work begins.

issues.summary: Match Play Game Assets
issues.description:
Create the assets that will be used in the Game Selection screen for the new Match Play game option (akin to what was done for Pentagon or Nassau)

:info:  Match play is the original game of golf, and probably the best. Match play pits individuals or teams against one another and each hole is its own contest. It is the most strategic duel in the game of golf, and the asset should reflect that.

- game .svg files to be used in game selection, leaderboard icons, et al

- this will be a Traditional game type (silver assets, such as Medalist)

- need at least one icon asset to be used in game selection, leaderboards, etc

- same sizing as the other SVG assets that were built out for Compete games

- game title

- Match Play

- game description short form

- The greatest duel in golf.

- game description long form

- The greatest duel in golf. Battle it out to see who can win the most holes.

comments.author: Dewan Kabir
comments.body:
We have found out that an Automation user QAParness , was being used via an automation test script to update the Temporary Facility Closure records in the Facility Settings page .

We were able to locate that , by investigating an involved Stored Procedure , which was looking into the facility Closure Map table , and saw that if there was an active record, then the tee times would not be returned by the stored procedure .

Upon removing any Facility Closure records in GNC for the affected facility , we were able to see the loaded inventory and complete the booking process .

As a precaution , we made QAParness Inactive in AWS DEV , and are looking into the teams which might be using that Automation user .

We also observed that , the tee times / inventory were bookable after the End Date of the Facility Closure schedule .

issues.summary: Support multiple Apple Pay cryptograms for a purchase
issues.description:
Update OrderCheckout endpoints to support the client passing two Apple Pay Cryptograms as PaymentMethods to buy a Tee time + GolfPass in the same transaction.

Apple Pay Docs: https://applepaydemo.apple.com/

- Apple Pay creates a cryptogram for each merchant and the client (web/app) will call out to Apple Pay to get the cryptograms and pass them to the API. Apple Pay calls this “Multi Merchant”.

- Need the ability to support a tee time + golfpass transaction where the client can pass in both but the user will only see one Apple Pay prompt with the combined values

- This should have the same validations as a credit card transaction where GolfPass is processed first

- This should have the same validations as a credit card transaction where if the tee time fails, the GolfPass can still succeed and purchasef

- Ensure that standalone tee time transactions function with all payment methods including Apple Pay

- Ensure that standalone GolfPass transactions function with all payment methods including Apple Pay

- Test with Hot Deals, Course times, Prepaid Course Times, Prepaid times with GN & GC revenue allocation all in combination with and without GolfPass

- This will require full regression of OrderCheckout API

- We need backwards compatibility to not break current OrderCheckout

- Confirm GolfPass Renewals work with Apple Pay as payment method

- Test Free Trial renewal to paid product with Apple Pay

- Confirm No Shows are functional for Apple Pay reservations

- Confirm Refunds are functional for Apple Pay

- Availability Info

- Auth Call

- Site can be null

- Secret can be null

- Response must return "access_token"

- Access token retrieved successfully

- Token stored securely

- Token expiration handling confirmed

"storeName": "Chicago",

"selectedFittings": [
"Iron"
],

- selectedFittings required (array)

"storeName": "Chicago",
"email": "test.customer@example.com",
"firstName": "Test",
"lastName": "Customer",
"phone": "3125550199",
"totalPrice": 350.00,

"serviceList": [
"Iron"
]
}

- storeName

- email (required)

- appointmentStartDateTime

- serviceList

Always Pass (Unmasked):

- Email

- Phone (if available)

- First name

- Last name

- Full name when available

Pricing:

- totalPrice passed

- Pricing structure exists in API (not yet live but available)

- No structural enhancement required later

---
- Cancellation

- Cancellation endpoint provided by vendor

- Uses Appointment Number

- Appointment number starts with “A”

- Confirm mapping to internal booking ID

- Validate cancellation response

- Validate error handling

---
- Sync & Inventory Rules

- Sync schedule: 0–60 days only

- Page 1 returns full 60-day window

- No polling beyond page 1

- Sync schedule aligned with other simulator interfaces

---
- Interface Configuration

Exposed Config Values:

- Store Name

- Selected Fitting (Free Text – e.g., Iron, Putter, etc.)

Interface Attributes Table (Hardcoded):

- Authorization configured

- Credentials stored securely

---
- Pricing & Notes Handling

Notes field must differentiate:

- Due at Course per player

- Due Online per player

Trade Logic Pattern:

request.TeeTime.IsTrade
? "GolfNow Trade Round: $0."
: $"Prepaid Course Round - Due at Course amount per player: {request.Pricing.DueAtCoursePerPlayer:C} - TeeTime Price: {request.Pricing.BaseSpecialRate:C}.";

- Matches Club Prophet formatting

- Consistent with other simulator interfaces

---
- Data Handling Requirements

- Always pass unmasked email

- Always pass unmasked phone (if available)

- Always pass full name (if available)

- Confirm no masking occurs in outbound payload

- Confirm PII compliance

---
- DevOps / Infrastructure

- Cache Manager instance request submitted

- Submitted prior to CORE release

- QA and Prod credentials configured

- Secrets stored securely

- Environment variables configured

- IP whitelisting confirmed (if required)

---
- Testing Checklist

Auth:

- Access token retrieved

- Expiration handled

GetFitting:

- Correct fittings returned per store

Availability:

- Returns 0–60 day window

- Page locked to 1

- Filtering by selected fitting works

Schedule:

- Appointment successfully created

- Pricing stored correctly

- Unmasked PII sent

- Time reflects correct local facility time

- Appointment number mapping correct

- Cancellation succeeds

issues.summary: Add Status to Send to CORE | Refund and Player Count Update Made via GNC Cause Pro to Remove Associated Order From Remaining Golfers for Send Order to Interface Orders
issues.description:
Issue:

Below are all tickets that were previously created for this issue.
https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/GN1S-4196
https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/CORE-12618
https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/GN1-15353
https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/GN1-18491

And most recently in https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/GN1-23179 , where partial resolution was gained.

However, in testing we found that when a refund is done via GNC, Player slot 1 is refunded first, as opposed to player slot 4. (left to right)

During cancellation process, player slot 4 is removed first (right to left)

NOTE: This same behavior is seen on EZRTS.

This is a Priority ticket for Support.

If a send order to interface booking contains more than one player and via GNC, the booking is updated from 4 players to 3 players and a refund is performed for a value equal to that one player, the tee sheet accurately shows 3 players, however the 3 players on the tee sheet no longer show as paid and are no longer associated to the closed order. The closed order also shows the the lead player on the order as being refunded, as opposed to the last player.

In this ticket, Desimo will mock up what the data will look like with a new Status field that will be sent to CORE.  Once this is discussed with Brian, CORE team will create a ticket on their side.

Acceptance Criteria:

Make necessary adjustments in data sent so that refunds are handled in a way that is consistent with cancellations.

Will this added field affect anything on EZRTS side?

- Please do regression for legacy smartplay workflow specifically prepaid workflow

issues.summary: Add Logic for Account Anniversary PFA Bonus Look Back Date
issues.description:
The business would like to add a restriction to the account anniversary PFA bonus that limits how far back we award the bonus.

Example: Business wants to limit bonus to accounts created on 1/1/2020 or later

- Customer A created account on 7/4/2023

- Customer A receives anniversary bonus on 7/4/2026

- Customer B created account on 1/1/2020

- Customer B receives anniversary bonus on 1/1/2026

- Customer C created account on 11/11/2017

- Customer C does not receive anniversary bonus on 11/11/2026

Note:

- The look back date should be configurable per campaign, not hard coded.

- The anniversary bonuses will be awarded moving forward, not retroactively

issues.summary: GNC UI - Points for Actions Campaign Page

Requirements:

Searching campaigns

- This should be its own dedicated page (similar to promo codes)

- ‘Create Campaign’ button in the top right corner

- ‘Search By:’ dropdown with the following values to choose from:

- Name

- ID

- Type

- Status

- Create Date

- Start Date

- End Date

- ‘Value:’ field with the appropriate type of input field depending on which ‘Search By’ option is selected

- Name - Input text (VARCHAR)

- ID - Input text

- Status - Dropdown

- Create Date - Date picker

- Start Date - Date picker

- End Date - Date picker

- ‘Search’ button

- Applicable results should be returned in the following format:

- ‘Edit’ and ‘Copy’ links

- Create Date

- ID

- Type

- Campaign Display Name

- Start Date

- End Date

- Status

- ‘Clear Search’ button

- Removes the search filter and returns all campaigns

Creating campaigns

- This should be its own dedicated page (similar to promo codes)

- The following fields will always be generated and required for all campaigns

- Create Date:

- Auto-populate with the following:

- Date

- Time

- Username

- Campaign Name:

- Default to blank value

- Input text field (VARCHAR)

- Character limit = 28

- Campaign Description:

- Default to blank value

- Input text field (VARCHAR)

- Action ID:

- This value will be auto-populated by the system after the campaign is created

- Campaign Duration:

- Default to blank values for all fields:

- Start Date

- Date picker

- End Date

- Date picker

- Time Zone

- Dropdown

- Start Time

- Input text

- End Time

- Input text

- Note: End date and end time must be greater than start date and time

- Action Details

- Action Type

- Dropdown

- Values

- Tee Time Bonus

- Profile Completion

- Account Creation & Anniversary

- GolfPass Membership

- The following campaign detail fields will be generated based on the selected Action Type

- Tee Time Bonus

- Is First Time Booker

- Checkbox

- Default to unchecked

- “First Time Booker” is defined as booking your first reservation since 2024

- This may change to lifetime with future enhancements

- Is GolfPass Member

- Checkbox

- Default to unchecked

- Has an active subscription with ProductTypeID = 9

- Type of Round

- Trade

- Checkbox

- Default to unchecked

- Course

- Checkbox

- Default to unchecked

- Type of Facility

- Golf Course

- Checkbox

- Default to unchecked

- Only applies to facilities that are not simulators

- Simulator

- Checkbox

- Default to unchecked

- Only applies to simulator facilities

- If no boxes are checked, assume all facility types are applicable

- Play Date/Time Range

- Tee Time Start Date

- Date Picker

- Default to blank value

- Limit to less than or equal to 1/1/2024

- Tee Time End Date

- Date Picker

- Default to blank value

- Tee Time Start Time

- Input text field

- Default to blank value

- Tee Time End Time

- Input text field

- Default to blank value

- Note: End date and end time must be greater than start date and time

- Time of Day

- Time of Day Start

- Input text field

- Default to blank value

- The time that the event was triggered must be equal to or after this configured start time (if no start time is provided, start of day is what this value should default to)

- Time of Day End

- Input text field

- Default to blank value

- The time that the event was triggered must be equal to or earlier than this configured end time (if no end time is provided, end of day is what this value should default to)

- Note: End time must be greater than start time

- Days Out Range

- Days Out Start

- Input text field

- Default to blank value

- Info: The number of days before play date (Day 0 = today)

- Days Out End

- Input text field

- Default to blank value

- Note: Days out end should be greater than days out start

- Minimum Number of Rounds

- Round Quantity

- Input text field

- Default to blank value

- At least one of the two, Minimum Number of Rounds or Minimum Number of Reservations, must be required and filled out in order for the Tee Time Bonus campaign to be saved and created

- If Number of Rounds is filled out, then Number of Reservations should be grayed out and uneditable

- Minimum Number of Reservations

- Reservation Quantity

- Input text field

- Default to blank value

- At least one of the two, Minimum Number of Rounds or Minimum Number of Reservations, must be required and filled out in order for the Tee Time Bonus campaign to be saved and created

- If Number of Reservations is filled out, then Number of Rounds should be grayed out and uneditable

- Checkbox

- Checkbox

- Default to unchecked

- Checkbox

- Inclusive Play Facility Set

- This should account for both the play course facilities rates and the master facility rate sets associated

- If play facility is inclusive, then it cannot be added to the exclusive list

- Selector tool that matches promo codes

- Default to zero PPIDs selected

- Limit to only PPIDs under ProductType 9

- If no owners are selected, then the action is available on all owners

- Hierarchy

- If no PPIDs are set, look for PID

- If no PID is set, look for ProductTypeID = 9

- Points Allotment

- Points Rewarded

- Input text field

- Default to blank value

- Make this field required for the campaign to be saved and created

- Max use per customer

- Input text field

- Default to the following values for each Action Type

- Tee Time Bonus

- Blank Value

- Default to 1

- This will limit fraud by preventing users from being able to add a phone number, get points, delete phone number, and then add it again and get more points

- Make this field required for the campaign to be saved and created

Editing Campaigns

- All previously filled out fields should be returned (no blank values if they were previously filled out)

- All rules around the fields required to create the campaign should still apply to editing the campaign

- Ex: Either the Minimum Number of Rounds or Minimum Number of Reservations must be filled out

- The Action ID value that was auto-populated upon saving the campaign should now be displayed

          2. Default to zero facilities selected

          3. Play facility with which the booking is allowed

            1. This should account for both the play course facilities rates and the master facility rate sets associated

          4. If play facility is inclusive, then it cannot be added to the exclusive list

        12. Exclusive Play Facility Set

          1. Selector tool that matches promo codes

          2. Default to zero facilities selected

          3. Play facility with which the booking is not allowed

            1. This should account for both the play course facilities rates and the master facility rate sets associated

          4. If play facility is exclusive, then it cannot be added to the inclusive list

        13. Owner Set

          1. Selector tool that matches promo codes

          2. Default to zero owners selected

          3. The assumption should be if no owner is selected, then the action is available for all owners

      2. Profile Completion

        1. Profile Field Completed

          1. First Name

            1. Checkbox

            2. Default to unchecked

          2. Last Name

            1. Checkbox

            2. Default to unchecked

          3. Birth Date

            1. Checkbox

            2. Default to unchecked

          4. Phone Number

            1. Checkbox

            2. Default to unchecked

          5. Address Line 1

            1. Checkbox

            2. Default to unchecked

          6. Country

            1. Checkbox

            2. Default to unchecked

          7. Preferred Language

            1. Checkbox

            2. Default to unchecked

        2. Owner Set

          1. Selector tool that matches promo codes

          2. Default to zero owners selected

          3. The assumption should be if no owner is selected, then the action is available for all owners

      3. Account Creation & Anniversary

        1. Initial Account Creation

          1. Checkbox

          2. Default to unchecked

        2. Annual Account Creation Anniversary

          1. Checkbox

          2. Default to unchecked

          3. This applies to the one year anniversary of the initial account creation

            1. Note: if max user per customer = 5, then this should apply to the first five years from the initial account creation

        3. Initial Creation and Annual Anniversary should not both be allowed in the same campaign

        4. Owner Set

          1. Selector tool that matches promo codes

          2. Default to zero owners selected

          3. The assumption should be if no owner is selected, then the action is available for all owners

      4. GolfPass Membership

        1. Membership Purchase Type

          1. Any Purchase of ProductTypeID 9

            1. Checkbox

            2. Default to unchecked

          2. 1st Purchase of ProductTypeID 9

            1. Checkbox

            2. Default to unchecked

          3. Renewal into ProductTypeID 9

            1. Checkbox

            2. Default to unchecked

        2. Annual Membership Anniversary

          1. Checkbox

          2. Default to unchecked

          3. This applies to the one year anniversary of the initial product purchase

        3. Applicable Product IDs

          1. Selector tool that matches promo codes

          2. Default to zero PIDs selected

          3. Limit to only PIDs under ProductType 9

        4. Applicable Product Price IDs

          1. Selector tool that matches promo codes

          2. Default to zero PPIDs selected

          3. Limit to only PPIDs under ProductType 9

        5. Owner Set

          1. Selector tool

          2. Default to zero owners selected

          3. If no owners are selected, then the action is available on all owners

        6. Hierarchy

          1. If no PPIDs are set, look for PID

          2. If no PID is set, look for ProductTypeID = 9

  4. Points Allotment

    1. Points Rewarded

      1. Input text field

      2. Default to blank value

      3. Make this field required for the campaign to be saved and created

    2. Max use per customer

      1. Input text field

      2. Default to the following values for each Action Type

        1. Tee Time Bonus

          1. Blank Value

        2. Profile Completion

          1. Default to 1

          2. Make it ‘Read Only’

            1. This will limit fraud by preventing users from being able to add a phone number, get points, delete phone number, and then add it again and get more points

      3. Make this field required for the campaign to be saved and created

    3. Max use per campaign

      1. Input text field

      2. Default to blank value

      3. Include a note next to the textbox that says “0 = unlimited”

      4. Make this field required for the campaign to be saved and created

    4. Status

      1. Default to ‘Inactive’

      2. Active (Published)

Editing Campaigns

  1. All previously filled out fields should be returned (no blank values if they were previously filled out)

  2. All rules around the fields required to create the campaign should still apply to editing the campaign

    1. Ex: Either the Minimum Number of Rounds or Minimum Number of Reservations must be filled out

  3. The Action ID value that was auto-populated upon saving the campaign should now be displayed

- API Details: TBD

issues.summary: Prepaid green fee full order refund partially failed in Pro but went through fully in the Financial Dashboard/GNC
issues.description:
Location: Angeles National GC

Issue:

A prepaid reservation for 2 golfers was on the course tee sheet for 10-DEC-2025 - Joseph J at 9:44am that staff attempted to perform a full refund for.  For some reason, Pro only recognizes that 1 of the green fees was refunded and one remained paid/available to be refunded.

Attempting to process the refund on the remaining time results in the error: “Unexpected error while refunding prepaid order. Response status code does not indicate success: 400 (Bad Request)”

Neither EPOS or Legacy can perform the refund:

The order details for  order 100479988974 show that only 1 of the green fees was refunded, however the Financial Dashboard and GNC show that it was refunded in full:

Transaction Report:

GNC Reservation Details:

https://golfnowcentral.com/Reservation/Edit/416665116

“View Reservation History” on the reservation in GNC:

The Prepaid Reservations Payments show it was refunded in full:

As does the FD:

Shannon confirmed that the refund looks to have been initiated within GNC.

Acceptance Criteria:

- Can we see the payload that GNC sent Pro regarding the refund?

- Any disconnect that might have caused the discrepancy?

- Why was the refund was only processed for one green fee in Pro and not the entire order?

- Why does attempting to refund the remaining green fee fail, despite the transaction already being refunded according to the FD/GNC reports?

- How can the reservation be updated in Pro so that it matches the FD/GNC?

issues.summary: Tee Time Credits - Investigate if they are reusable after reservation is cancelled
issues.description:
Request :

Could you book a tee time using one of the $10 monthly promo codes, cancel the tee time, and then let me know if the promo code becomes available again to be used for a different tee time?
issues.descriptionHtml:
Request :

Could you book a tee time using one of the $10 monthly promo codes, cancel the tee time, and then let me know if the promo code becomes available again to be used for a different tee time?

comments.author: Dewan Kabir
comments.body:
Research :

We initially found our that in AWS DEV , the Strored Procedure : StoredProcedure [Merchandise].[GetUserSubscriptionsToProcess]  had a hard coded Customer Number being passed through in it , so when ever we ran the Subscription Item Processor task , it was being executed with only that Customer Record.

After we removed that hard coded data , we ran the proc , and saw the tons of staged data , which were ready to be processed , and so after executing the task , we saw that the records were being processed as expected , along side the emails for the Hot Deal Tee Time Credit Promo Codes coming through as well .

Once the task completed , we started testing with our target user , and saw that the promo code which was generated for the new user was associated with a promo code campaign which already expired .

After updating that promo code campaign , we started to test the promo code on a trade tee time , and saw regardless of the booking going through GNC / Reservation Service or API 2.1 , once the booking was cancelled , the tee time credit promo code still had the “ Claimed “ status .
comments.bodyHtml:
Research :

We initially found our that in AWS DEV , the Strored Procedure : StoredProcedure [Merchandise].[GetUserSubscriptionsToProcess] had a hard coded Customer Number being passed through in it , so when ever we ran the Subscription Item Processor task , it was being executed with only that Customer Record.

After we removed that hard coded data , we ran the proc , and saw the tons of staged data , which were ready to be processed , and so after executing the task , we saw that the records were being processed as expected , along side the emails for the Hot Deal Tee Time Credit Promo Codes coming through as well .

Once the task completed , we started testing with our target user , and saw that the promo code which was generated for the new user was associated with a promo code campaign which already expired .

After updating that promo code campaign , we started to test the promo code on a trade tee time , and saw regardless of the booking going through GNC / Reservation Service or API 2.1 , once the booking was cancelled , the tee time credit promo code still had the “ Claimed “ status .

issues.summary: Investigate GolfNow Tax Calculation Behavior and Share Vertex Request/Response Data with Commerce
issues.description:
Tax calculation behavior was observed to differ slightly between the GolfNow platform and the Commerce platform. To help diagnose and understand these discrepancies, an investigation was performed into how tax was being calculated on the GolfNow side.

As part of this effort, the Vertex tax request and response objects generated by GolfNow were captured and shared with the Commerce team. This information was provided to support troubleshooting efforts and to help identify where and why the tax calculation behavior between the two platforms may be diverging.

issues.summary: Auto Adjust '1 Day Out' Does Not Block Same Day Inventory and 2 day out blocks are intermittently failing
issues.description:
Summary

As a Revenue Manager, I would expect Auto Adjust that is set to ‘1 Day Out’ to block same day inventory. Instead, what is currently happening is that same day inventory is not blocked unless the AA schedule is updated from ‘1 Day Out’ to ’23 Hours Out’.

Steps to Recreate

- GNC -> Inventory -> Auto Adjust Schedules

- Select a Trade facility, such as .com/Phoenix (FID 47)

- Create an AA schedule for 1 day out

- Upload same day inventory with the 1 day AA schedule and check Update Tee Times. You will see the inventory is available for booking.

- Go back to the 1 day out schedule, update it to 23 hours out, and check UTT again. Same day inventory will now be blocked.

Expected Result

The expected result is that a rate set with an Auto Adjust schedule of 1 day out will show the same day inventory as being blocked because it is within the range of one day/24 hours.

---
It is also being reported that 2 Day Out blocks on course times are not working. This is happening on simulators. I dont think the fact that it is a SIM is causing this it just happens to be where most are being used. Unlike 1 day out blocks, the limit in GNC is 24 so there is no workaround to do 47 hours. Could that be a short term solution to increase the GNC to allow 48 hours?

- This is being reported at all the Next Golf facilities in prod

comments.author: Luis Vallejo Mursuli
comments.body:
@Dewan Kabir

For this one, we couldn’t test directly in our dev environment because we weren’t able to make a valid call to the Vendor service, which is required to get the value that’s causing the error (conversion error). Instead, we fixed it on our side since we located the exact place where this is happening. It’s also worth mentioning that we couldn’t confirm whether this is specifically related to a user trying to book Military Tee Times.

Long story short, this issue in prod is caused when the Reservation service makes a call to the Vendor service, which proxies a call to a G1 external link (the source of the wrong value).

Our fix was on our side to avoid the conversion issue we see in the logs from the attached snapshot (from string to Int32). When conversion isn’t possible, we now use 1 as a fallback value. No database changes were required.

Where to look: the CRM.Reservation.ReservationSlot table. Why: that’s where we store this information when we successfully call the Vendor service. In the attached image, you can see the column highlighted where the conversion error occurs. In the second table (from our environment), you can see many values that are incorrect based on what this column represents (it should be a value in the range 1 to 4). I imagine that since this is just a dev environment, it’s acceptable to see bad data, but it’s worth checking in prod what values this query is actually returning.

In conclusion, we were receiving an invalid value from the call to the Vendor service, and, in this specific case, it was a value outside the valid range for the Int32 data type (the reason for the issue seen in the logs). From a business perspective, this number should always be in the range 1 to 4. Our solution was to avoid raising an exception due to the conversion issue and instead use 1 as a fallback value.

The best way to test this is to try creating a reservation for the specified user, making sure you’re hitting a valid external link (via the Vendor service).

issues.summary: Compete Email production deployment verification
issues.description:
With the completion of https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/CORE-14034 dev has moved the compete email distribution process off of the phx-notification-api and onto the FinTech managed Email API.

In order to do this we need to deploy our updates to golfnow-compete-notification-consumer but it was discovered that this service was never migrated to the AWS deployment pipeline in production and is still being deployed and controlled over in GCP.

This ticket will be used on the QA side for verifying https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/CORE-14034 fixes are pushed to production when the AWS pipeline is fixed. Or this ticket will be converted into a workable ticket if determined CORE dev support is need to resolve this issue.

comments.author: Alex McNay
comments.body:
Update from Niamh Goodwin -

I was able to confirm with our contractors and internal team that this consumer was originally set up during the major migrations. All AWS CI/CD pipelines are in place across environments; however, the production cutover was never tested and had to be put on hold to prioritise more urgent work.

Although a GKE production path still exists (for the current GKE cluster running in production), it appears the previous workflow was to deploy to Kubernetes staging and, once QA signed off, reuse that same image for production rather than building a dedicated production image.

Unfortunately, this flow is no longer viable. Our dev and staging pipelines are now AWS-only, and images are pushed to ECR rather than GCR or GAR.

As a result, we can’t move forward with changes to this consumer until the team is able to complete the AWS production cutover. They’re currently on a tight timeline with larger applications, but I’ll make sure to check in periodically so this doesn’t get lost.

comments.author: Joshua Marquess
comments.body:
CORE workflow for EZ1 issues:

- CORE calls GetUserRegistration - pass USERID GUID as it is in database and contact ID does not exist proceed to AddMember

- If no contactID in response, we recall all UPPER Case

- If still no contactID in response, we call AddMember

- If no contactID, proceed to AddMember (-1 or 50003 or 500002)

- If -1 or 500003 or 500002 on response. Retry AddMember with all UPPER CASE

- If exception again, we fail call and process EZL1 error

Post meeting notes:
CORE workflow is correct.

EZL team is looking into recent examples to find out more. Will update ticket post-findings

issues.summary: EZL Cart Fee Issue
issues.description:
Whenever a cart fee is added into GNC Configure Rate sets, we send the Green fee only as the rate to the EZTP tee sheet. The request is send over the total price with cart so that it can show up correctly in their slot breakout and pricing notes fields.

Richter Park - FID 5789

This course is just one example of the logic that is causing the wrong rate to show in EZTP.

When Cart Fee is being used (in this case $20), GNC is splitting the total price (GF + CF) up into 2 values and sending the wrong Green Fee amount over to EZTP. For example, a $97 rate was booked that includes the $20 rate fee, but EZTP reflects a $77 rate (cart fee removed). We need the logic updated so that the price booked shows exactly the same on EZTP.

Res 405196814

issues.summary: Support Customer Notes in Commerce API by Passing customerNotes Metadata Through to GolfNow Reservation Workflow
issues.description:
We need to enhance the Commerce → GolfNow reservation workflow to support customer-supplied notes entered during checkout. Currently, the Commerce API includes these notes in the item’s Metadata object under the customerNotes key, but the GolfNow API reservation workflow does not receive or process this value.

This ticket will introduce end-to-end handling of customer notes by:

Scope of Work

- Read the customerNotes metadata field from the Commerce API Item.Metadata object.

- Ensure this value is included when constructing the reservation request payload sent to the GolfNow API.

- Identify the correct field/property within the GolfNow API reservation workflow to map these notes into (e.g., reservation-level metadata or a dedicated customer notes field).

Acceptance Criteria

- Customer notes entered in Commerce successfully appear on the GolfNow reservation.

- Notes are visible in downstream systems that rely on GolfNow reservation data.

- Notes are passed to the tee sheet appended to the other system notes we pass to the teesheet

- Do not overwrite any existing logic for notes that we pass to the teesheet

- Replicated behavior for notes field on Add Reservation call in Transparent Redirect

issues.summary: Mini-Spike: Online Booking | Not All Player Slots with Cart Get the Cart Toggle Enabled within the Tee Time Modal
issues.description:
Location: Dufferin Glen (FID 8316)
Issue:

When online bookings are made where a cart is included, it seems that not all of the player slots are having the got toggle enabled within the tee time modal, when they should.

Below is the the write up from Support:

Reservation 403892001 was booked for 4 players and is supposed to include a cart for each player, however the G1 sheet only shows a Cart Included for 2 of the 4 players (See screenshot). They were charged for cart included on each player as well. We previously escalated this to the CORE team on [TTSUPPORT-7075] Carts Not Included on G1 Tee Sheet - GolfNow  but they advised us that the CORE system doesn’t adjust the cart count so they think it was adjusted by the interface with Pro.

Why did this booking only have 2 carts instead of 1 per player?

Steps to Reproduce:

Tested in Production at Golfnow Links East.

Utilized the GolfNow Links East 18 Holes rateset, which has a cart included, is not prepaid and does not have Send order to Interface Enabled.

Made all bookings via https://golfnow-links-east.book.teeitup.com/?course=17597&date=2025-07-02&max=9999

Made a booking for a single, two-some, three-some and four-some. All bookings made on 7/3/2025

Single: Reservation #408412801 8:00am 7/3/2025

Two-some: Reservation #408412116 7:10am 7/3/2025

Three-some: Reservation #408412353 7:20am 7/3/2025

Four-some: Reservation #408411636 7:00am 7/3/2025

The single booking has the cart toggle enabled as expected.

The two-some shows the first player slot with the cart toggle enabled, but the second player slot has the cart toggle disabled

The three-some shows the first two player slots with the cart toggle enabled, but the third player slot has the cart toggle disabled

The four-some shows the first two player slots with the cart toggle enabled, but the third and fourth player slots have the toggle disabled

However, all player slots show the cart icon on the tee sheet.

Actual Results:d

Not all of the player slots in these bookings have the cart toggle enabled.

Expected Results:

All player slots have the cart toggle enabled.

Acceptance Criteria:

If a greens fee/rate set is set up to have a cart associated, then all player slots being booked should have the cart toggle enabled within the tee time modal.

Product Notes

For the avoidance of doubt, all players on a time slot that are associated to a green fee rate that includes a cart should have the toggle enabled.

It is somewhat counterintuitive since a user may be inclined to think all players with the toggle enabled should receive a cart. In reality the toggle just reflects if a cart is included in the player green fee and has no bearing on the number of carts applied.

Physical carts available for players on a time slot is handled by the cart counter which in almost all cases, when a green fee rate includes a cart, applies the logic:

- Bookings for 1 or 2 players will be granted no more than 1 cart.

- Bookings for 3 or 4 players will be granted no more than 2 carts.

A club set up with 20 carts available has been tested to ensure a booking for 4 players with a green fee inclusive of a cart and the cart toggle enabled for all players does not negatively affect the cart counter balance. Cart count correctly changed to 18, even though all players had the cart toggle enabled.

comments.author: Pierce McGeough
comments.body:
Hi @Andrew Lounsberry,

I dug into this and there are a few interacting pieces.

I don’t have the US payload yet, so this is based on diving into code paths. Marketing‑API bookings /golfchannel/golfchannel_golf_interface.php validate Buggies as ''|0|1|2, so anything above 2 will throw an error. That means GolfNow/Marketing‑API channels can never store more than 2 buggies per tee time.

The tee time stores a Buggies count against a booking. So if Buggies is capped at 2, only two player slots show the cart toggle even if all four players paid a cart‑included rate.

RTS behaves differently because it can set per‑slot has_buggy directly. This allows RTS to have 4 Buggies for 4 players. On G1, the cart counter still allocates only 2 carts for 4 players (shared logic), so toggles don’t inflate cart inventory.

Potential fixes. I see two options:

Option A
Keep the cap at 2 and update systems using GNC to indicate carts are shared for 3–4 player bookings on cart‑included rates. This aligns with the product note “cart included in fee,” not assigned carts.

Likely changes required

- GNC UI messaging/labels to explain shared carts

Option B
Update code to allow 4 buggies. This would require changes across multiple systems.

Likely changes required

- Marketing API validation to allow 0–4

- Any downstream systems in GNC/BRS that expect max 2, would need updating

- Potential others

issues.summary: Refund and Player Count Update Made via GNC Cause Pro to Remove Associated Order From Remaining Golfers for Send Order to Interface Orders
issues.description:
Issue:

Below are all tickets that were previously created for this issue.
https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/GN1S-4196
https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/CORE-12618
https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/GN1-15353
https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/GN1-18491

NOTE: This same behavior is seen on EZRTS.

This is a Priority ticket for Support.

If a send order to interface booking contains more than one player and via GNC, the booking is updated from 4 players to 3 players and a refund is performed for a value equal to that one player, the tee sheet accurately shows 3 players, however the 3 players on the tee sheet no longer show as paid and are no longer associated to the closed order. The closed order also shows the the lead player on the order as being refunded, as opposed to the last player.

Steps to Reproduce:

- In a BE which is configured for prepaid reservations and which allows you to prepay for all four golfers (ie. Enable Member Booking Limit must be turned off - I turned it off in this BE for testing and have since turned it back on), and which has “Send Order to Interface” enabled on the rate set, reserve and prepay for a foursome. This will produce their reservation on the tee sheet and a completed order reflecting the prepayment in G1.

- Log into GNC, search for and access the reservation you just made in Step 1.

- Click the Facility name under Selected Facility to open the search box.

- Search for and select the facility the BE you tested with uses.

- Click Customers > Reservations

- Narrow the date range down to the date when you booked your reservation in step 1 (optionally, you can also use the Rate Set dropdown menu to narrow your results down even further) and click Search

- Locate your test reservation among the results and click Edit in the Reservation column.

- Still in GNC, reduce the player count to 3.

- Open the Players dropdown and select 3.

- Open the Cancellation Reason dropdown that is revealed, select a reason.

- Click Save Players

- Still in GNC, partially refund the green fee.

- In the Transaction History box in GNC check the box to the left of your original prepayment.

- Open the Refund Reason dropdown and select an option.

- In the Manual Transaction section, enter a value corresponding to one quarter of your original prepayment into the Amount field.

- Click Process Credit Card.

- Check your G1 Tee Sheet.

Actual Results:

Pro tee sheet correctly removes player slot 4, however, the 3 remaining player slots no longer show as being paid and are not associated with the closed order.

The closed order also shows the the lead player on the order as being refunded, as opposed to the last player.

Expected Results:

The tee sheet shows the 3 remaining players and still shows them as being paid with the closed order still associated with each of the 3 player slots.

The closed order should show player slot 4 being refunded as opposed to the lead player.

Acceptance Criteria:

On 11/19/2025, we met with CORE and determined the following:
We found that this is an edge case that happens specifically in GNC with separate API calls for the cancellation and refund separately and not on BRS teesheet for partial refunds/cancellations - please work with Engineer GN.com when API 2.1 processes them both together.

G1 team is going to find a way to utilize the data we are getting to resolve this issue so that any remaining player slots do not lose the association with the closed order and remain as paid on the tee sheet.  Also, ensure we show the correct player as being refunded on the closed order.

If a send order to interface booking contains more than one player and via GNC, the booking is updated from 4 players to 3 players and a refund is performed for a value equal to that one player, the tee sheet accurately shows 3 players, however the 3 players on the tee sheet no longer show as paid and are no longer associated to the closed order. The closed order also shows the the lead player on the order as being refunded, as opposed to the last player.

Steps to Reproduce:

  1. In a BE which is configured for prepaid reservations and which allows you to prepay for all four golfers (ie. Enable Member Booking Limit must be turned off - I turned it off in this BE for testing and have since turned it back on), and which has “Send Order to Interface” enabled on the rate set, reserve and prepay for a foursome. This will produce their reservation on the tee sheet and a completed order reflecting the prepayment in G1.

  2. Log into GNC, search for and access the reservation you just made in Step 1.

    1. Click the Facility name under Selected Facility to open the search box.

    2. Search for and select the facility the BE you tested with uses.

    3. Click Customers > Reservations

    4. Narrow the date range down to the date when you booked your reservation in step 1 (optionally, you can also use the Rate Set dropdown menu to narrow your results down even further) and click Search

    5. Locate your test reservation among the results and click Edit in the Reservation column.

  3. Still in GNC, reduce the player count to 3.

    1. Open the Players dropdown and select 3.

    2. Open the Cancellation Reason dropdown that is revealed, select a reason.

    3. Click Save Players

  4. Still in GNC, partially refund the green fee.

    1. In the Transaction History box in GNC check the box to the left of your original prepayment.

    2. Open the Refund Reason dropdown and select an option.

    3. In the Manual Transaction section, enter a value corresponding to one quarter of your original prepayment into the Amount field.

    4. Click Process Credit Card.

  5. Check your G1 Tee Sheet.

Actual Results:

Pro tee sheet correctly removes player slot 4, however, the 3 remaining player slots no longer show as being paid and are not associated with the closed order.

The closed order also shows the the lead player on the order as being refunded, as opposed to the last player.

Expected Results:

The tee sheet shows the 3 remaining players and still shows them as being paid with the closed order still associated with each of the 3 player slots.

The closed order should show player slot 4 being refunded as opposed to the lead player.

Acceptance Criteria:

On 11/19/2025, we met with CORE and determined the following:
We found that this is an edge case that happens specifically in GNC with separate API calls for the cancellation and refund separately and not on BRS teesheet for partial refunds/cancellations - please work with Engineer GN.com when API 2.1 processes them both together.

G1 team is going to find a way to utilize the data we are getting to resolve this issue so that any remaining player slots do not lose the association with the closed order and remain as paid on the tee sheet. Also, ensure we show the correct player as being refunded on the closed order.

issues.summary: Fix Commerce Workflow Failure When No Payment Is Due Online and No Customer Wallet Exists
issues.description:
Problem

The Commerce reservation workflow fails when nothing is due online and the customer does not have a wallet created with payment methods.

In this scenario, the workflow appears to still require a payment method to be present, even though no payment is required. This impacts both guest users and authenticated customers who do not yet have a wallet or saved payment methods.

Expected Behavior

When the total due online amount is $0.00, the Commerce workflow should allow the reservation to complete successfully without requiring a customer wallet or payment method.

Additional Context

This same scenario works correctly in the Transparent Redirect flow, where reservations with no amount due online are allowed to proceed even when no wallet or payment methods exist.

Because of this, it may be helpful to review how the Transparent Redirect flow handles zero-due reservations and align the Commerce workflow behavior accordingly.

Impact

- Blocks valid reservations when no payment is required

- Affects both guest and authenticated customers without wallets

- Creates inconsistent behavior between Commerce and Transparent Redirect flows

issues.summary: Improve Robustness of Cached Invoice Removal During Item Removal
issues.description:
The Remove Item endpoint should be improved to more reliably clear cached invoice data when items are removed from a cart.

While stale invoice data is not currently causing functional issues, cached invoices may remain in the system longer than necessary after item removal. The Remove Item flow should be updated to proactively clear invoice cache entries as soon as possible, across a wider set of scenarios.

The desired outcome is improved cache hygiene and more consistent cleanup of invoice data during item removal, helping ensure the system remains efficient and avoids unnecessary retention of cached invoices.

comments.author: Tyler Olechnowicz
comments.body:
QA

Previously, invoices were not able to be removed from the cache unless the OrderInvoiceResponseCacheKey property was present in the item metadata. This property only gets added to the metadata after the GenerateDistributions endpoint is executed.

Execute the CreateInvoice endpoint and then execute the RemoveItem endpoint and make sure that the invoice is removed from the cache. You will know that the invoice is removed from the cache because re-executing the CreateInvoice endpoint will take the normal amount of time instead of being lightening quick.

The cache key is built off of these parameters, so make sure that these values are the same for both the CreateInvoice and RemoveItem calls:

cacheKeyToRemove = RedisKeyBuilder.BuildGolfNowInvoiceKey<OrderInvoiceResponse>(
request.CartKey,
request.Item.CartItemKey,
clientTokenClaims.ClientUsername,
clientTokenClaims.ChannelId,
teeTimeId,
request.UserAccount.EmailAddress,
request.Item.Quantity,
request.Item.UnitPrice.Amount);

issues.summary: Update RefundOrderInInterfaceActivity to Send Payment Method Type and Transaction ID from Payment Processing API to Vendor Service
issues.description:
Problem

Refunds are successfully processed through the Payments system. However, the notification we send to Vendor Service after a refund does not include all of the information Vendor Service needs to properly reflect the refund.

When PaymentMethodKey-based payments are used, the refund notification relies on our internal payment method type, which does not represent the actual underlying payment method used by Payments. In addition, the refund confirmation reference returned by Payments is not included in the notification.

As a result, refunds complete successfully on our side, but Vendor Service cannot reliably associate or represent the refund in their system.

---
Desired Outcome

Enhance the refund notification sent to Vendor Service so that, when applicable:

- The underlying payment method type used by Payments is included

- The refund transaction identifier is included

- The refund confirmation reference is included

This will allow Vendor Service to correctly reflect and reconcile refunds without changing the existing refund execution flow.

---
Payment Method Handling

When a PaymentMethodKey-based payment is involved:

- The underlying payment method type should be resolved using the Payment Processing API

- The resolved value should be mapped to the payment method format expected by Vendor Service

- If an underlying payment method type is not available, existing internal payment type behavior should be preserved

Vendor Service recognizes the following payment method values:

- "credit" or "creditcard"

- "accountbalance"

- "g1payment"

- Any other value is treated as "unknown"

---
Metadata Requirements

The refund notification must include the following values in the RefundItem.Metadata dictionary:

- TransactionID
Populated with the refund transaction ID returned by the Payment Processing API

- RefundConfirmationID
Populated with the refund confirmation reference returned by Payments (PNREF)

---
Scope

- Update the Vendor Service refund notification built in RefundOrderInInterfaceActivity

- Resolve and populate the underlying payment method type when available

- Populate RefundItem.PaymentMethod using the resolved payment method mapping

- Populate RefundItem.Metadata["TransactionID"] with the refund transaction ID

- Populate RefundItem.Metadata["RefundConfirmationID"] with the refund confirmation reference

- Preserve existing refund execution behavior

issues.summary: Account Creation PFA Bonus Awarded for Account Updates
issues.description:
After analyzing the test data from the GP loyalty Points for Actions campaigns, we found some users were awarded the account creation bonus for account updates.

Example:

- CustomerID {1f8ff92c-11d2-4c73-af45-1cbf4569842f}

- Account created 06/13/13

- Loyalty PFA go-live 10/29/25

- Customer password hash updated 11/26/25

- Account creation bonus awarded 11/26/25

- Expectation: Account creation bonus should not have been awarded because the customer’s account was already created and active

Additional scenarios:

- Guest account converted to customer account

- Bonus should be awarded

- Guest wallet converted to customer wallet

- Bonus should not be awarded

- Password updated

- Bonus should not be awarded

comments.author: Yoel Martin Pardo
comments.body:
QA: The only way that we found a way to recreate the issue was calling the Add Customer endpoint with an Inactive customer account.

In order to validate the scenarios above, please follow the steps above:

1- Create a customer account using Add Customer endpoint.

2- Get the customer Id and run query above on Loyalty database:

SELECT * FROM [LoyaltyActions].[ActionQueue] WHERE CustomerId = 'CustomerId'

You should see a record with ActionTypeId = 4

3- Delete the record.

DELETE [LoyaltyActions].[ActionQueue] WHERE CustomerId = 'CustomerId'

4- Run Update Customer endpoint and check loyalty query again. You should not see any new record.

5- Duplicate Add Account endpoint and replace email and username with the data for the customer that you are testing with and run endpoint.

You should get an error saying customer already exists.

6- Update customer status be Inactive:

UPDATE CRMcustomer SET CStatus = 'Inactive' WHERE CustomerNumber = 'CustomerNumber'

7- Run Add Customer endpoint again.

You should get a 200k response and you should not see a new record on the loyalty table. The record should only be created when you are adding a new customer or when converting a guest to customer account.

In order to test convert guest to customer account, please use the Convert to Customer endpoint and also the Add Customer endpoint.

issues.summary: Disable Swagger UI  and ReDoc and API Documentation in Production Environment
issues.description:
Swagger UI and ReDoc documentation are currently enabled across all environments. For security and best-practice reasons, we should disable Swagger and ReDoc in the Production environment while keeping it available in Development, Staging, and other non-production deployments.

This update will ensure that:

- Swagger UI and ReDoc are not accessible in Production.

- These tools remain fully enabled in non-production environments for development, debugging, and QA testing.

- URL rewrite rules that redirect the root path to /swagger do not execute in Production.

Acceptance Criteria

- Swagger UI and ReDoc are not available in Production.

- /swagger, /swagger/index.html, and /redoc return 404 or do not map routes in Production.

- Root URL rewrite to Swagger is disabled in Production.

- Non-production environments still fully support Swagger and ReDoc pages.

issues.summary: Enhance Post Score logic to check Total, Front and Back Rating Availability
issues.description:
Results from research of https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/CFE-1670

:question: How can we make sure a user knows whether they’re allowed to post an 18 hole score, a 10-17 hole score, or a 9 hole score based on the USGA rating data available to us?

- we always load an 18 hole scorecard on Compete, but users may only be able to post for 9 holes, even if they’ve scored more

- this is a result of USGA tee marker data only containing “Front” half (1-9 holes) rating and slope data

Desired UX:

- a user can save a scorecard for any course we have in inventory, no problem (9, 10-17, 18)

- when they go to post a score, we need to know what ratings we have available

- Total

- Front

- Back

:check_mark:  Acceptance Criteria

- if we are missing “Back” rating and slope, we can only post the scores for 1-9 as a 9-hole round, and must alert user

- post holesScored = 9 and side = front for holes 1-9

- if we have Total, Front and Back ratings for the teemarker:

- we will ALWAYS post an 18 hole score when we have all 18 scores

- holesScored = 18 and side = All18

- we will ALWAYS post 10-17 holes scored when we have 10-17 holes scored

- holes scored = 10_17 and side = All18

@Andre Gamboa @Alex McNay please correct variable names and values above if they differ from Graph

:bookmark:  Please link Swagger and/or other documentation created as part of this effort

Link:

This ensures the front-end is armed with information they need for linked dependencies.

STR:

- score a full 18 hole round on the Bobby Jones Magnolia course - Id 1808

- Attempt to post the score to the USGA using the All18 tee set

- You’ll get an error saying the course is only able to post a 9 hole score

- The issue is centers around the fact that this 9 hole course doesn’t have a Back-9 holeRange and hasn’t account for an 18 hole round with it’s Total holeRange, which is just a duplicate of the Front-9 slope and rating

Query to show all the TeeMarkers that have a Front-9 (1) rating equal to their Total/18 Hole (3) rating. Meaning that they are on a 9 hole course that isn’t setup to score an 18 hole scorecard

SELECT Distinct(t1.TeeMarkerId)
FROM GolfCourse.TeeMarkerRating t1
JOIN GolfCourse.TeeMarkerRating t2
ON t1.teeMarkerId = t2.teeMarkerId
WHERE t1.Rating = t2.Rating AND t1.holeRange = 1 AND t2.holeRange = 3;

issues.summary: Accepting a USGA account link request sets all DB values to 3
issues.description:
:question: How can we sever the USGA Golfer ID from the Compete CustomerID so that a future GPA Access Approval does not trigger a link for PREVIOUS/REVOKED Customers?

Backend Research ticket for the issue below

If a user approves a link to a USGA account, and that USGA account was originally linked to another Compete user, both users will get their status updated to 3 - accepted. This is because we don’t have a way to know the difference between multiple USGA records in the golfer.accessRequest table that have the same USGA email and USGA golferId.

STR

- create a user in compete

- link that user to a USGA account

- unlink that compete user from that USGA account

- create a second user in compete

- link the same USGA account to the second compete user

- we will see both compete account are actively linked to the same USGA account
